[Investigation Nos. 701-TA-473 and 731-TA-1173 (Third Review)]
United States International Trade Commission.
The Commission hereby gives notice of the scheduling of expedited reviews pursuant to the Tariff Act of 1930 (“the Act”) to determine whether revocation of the countervailing and the antidumping duty orders on potassium phosphate salts from China would be likely to lead to continuation or recurrence of material injury within a reasonably foreseeable time.
Julie Duffy (202) 708-2579, Office of Investigations, U.S. International Trade Commission, 500 E Street SW, Washington, DC 20436. Hearing-impaired persons can obtain information on this matter by contacting the Commission's TDD terminal on 202-205-1810. Persons with mobility impairments who will need special assistance in gaining access to the Commission should contact the Office of the Secretary at 202-205-2000. General information concerning the Commission may also be obtained by accessing its internet server ( https://www.usitc.gov). The public record for this proceeding may be viewed on the Commission's electronic docket (EDIS) at https://edis.usitc.gov.
Background. —On September 4, 2026, the Commission determined that the domestic interested party group response to its notice of institution (91 FR 32445, June 1, 2026) of the subject ( printed page 74195) five-year reviews was adequate and that the respondent interested party group response was inadequate. The Commission did not find any other circumstances that would warrant conducting full reviews.[1] Accordingly, the Commission determined that it would conduct expedited reviews pursuant to section 751(c)(3) of the Act (19 U.S.C. 1675(c)(3)).
For further information concerning the conduct of these reviews and rules of general application, consult the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure, part 201, subparts A and B (19 CFR part 201), and part 207, subparts A, D, E, and F (19 CFR part 207).
Staff report. —A staff report containing information concerning the subject matter of the reviews has been placed in the nonpublic record, and will be made available to persons on the Administrative Protective Order service list for these reviews on November 17, 2026. A public version will be issued thereafter, pursuant to § 207.62(d)(4) of the Commission's rules.
Written submissions. —As provided in § 207.62(d) of the Commission's rules, interested parties that are parties to the reviews and that have provided individually adequate responses to the notice of institution,[2] and any party other than an interested party to the reviews may file written comments with the Secretary on what determination the Commission should reach in the reviews. Comments are due on or before November 24, 2026 and may not contain new factual information. Any person that is neither a party to the five-year reviews nor an interested party may submit a brief written statement (which shall not contain any new factual information) pertinent to the reviews by November 24, 2026. However, should the Department of Commerce (“Commerce”) extend the time limit for its completion of the final results of its reviews, the deadline for comments (which may not contain new factual information) on Commerce's final results is three business days after the issuance of Commerce's results. If comments contain business proprietary information (BPI), they must conform with the requirements of §§ 201.6, 207.3, and 207.7 of the Commission's rules. The Commission's Handbook on Filing Procedures, available on the Commission's website at https://www.usitc.gov/​documents/​handbook_​on_​filing_​procedures.pdf, elaborates upon the Commission's procedures with respect to filings.
In accordance with §§ 201.16(c) and 207.3 of the rules, each document filed by a party to the reviews must be served on all other parties to the reviews (as identified by either the public or BPI service list), and a certificate of service must be timely filed. The Secretary will not accept a document for filing without a certificate of service.
Determinations. —The Commission has determined these reviews are extraordinarily complicated and therefore has determined to exercise its authority to extend the review period by up to 90 days pursuant to 19 U.S.C. 1675(c)(5)(B).
Authority: These reviews are being conducted under authority of title VII of the Tariff Act of 1930; this notice is published pursuant to § 207.62 of the Commission's rules.
By order of the Commission.
Issued: November 16, 2026.

content:
圖為2026年1月15日，一架美國航空（American Airlines）的飛機在伊利諾伊州芝加哥奧黑爾國際機場（Chicago O'Hare International Airport）滑行。(Daniel SLIM/AFP via Getty Images)
【大紀元2026年11月18日訊】（大紀元記者吳瑞昌綜合報導）週二（11月17日），美國聯邦法官裁定，被控替中共拍攝芝加哥飛機和物流樞紐照片、並向調查人員撒謊的中國公民曾偉恆（Weiheng Zeng，音譯），在審判前必須繼續羈押。
據哥倫比亞廣播公司（CBS）報導，駐底特律（Detroit）的聯邦治安法官金伯利·奧爾特曼（Kimberly Altman）駁回了曾偉恆律師的請求。其律師團隊原本希望讓他交保，並在案件審理期間回到加拿大生活。
另外，美國司法部表示，曾偉恆的家人願意「支付本法院可能設定的任何保釋金」，甚至可以在美國買一套公寓，讓他交保後住在那裡。曾偉恆目前是加拿大安大略省滑鐵盧大學（University of Waterloo）的本科生。
據美國密西根州東區地方法院（U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan）的文件，聯邦大陪審團於11月5日起訴曾偉恆一項「向政府機構作虛假陳述」罪名。
曾偉恆本月早些時候作無罪抗辯。他並未因拍攝飛機照片被起訴，被指控的是向調查人員撒謊。
起訴書指出，8月23日，曾偉恆在底特律大使橋（Ambassador Bridge）口岸接受美國海關與邊境保護局（CBP）官員詢問時聲稱，他今年4月入境美國、擅闖奧黑爾國際機場（O'Hare International Airport）的聯邦快遞（FedEx）場地，只是「業餘愛好」。
聯邦調查局（FBI）探員的宣誓書（affidavit）指出，曾偉恆今年4月在奧黑爾機場的聯邦快遞設施內拍照，還爬上停放的叉車，並試圖打開上鎖的拖車。司法部表示，監控錄像顯示曾偉恆試圖打開一個集裝箱，並利用叉車站在更高處進行拍攝。
調查人員後來發現，現場出現過一輛掛安大略省車牌的深藍色克萊斯勒（Chrysler）廂型車，並把這輛車與曾偉恆聯繫起來。
據加拿大電視網新聞（CTV News）引述法庭文件報導，曾偉恆近4年前取得美國簽證，此後大約入境美國24次。8月23日，他開著同一輛廂型車，從加拿大經大使橋入境美國時，因為4月的事件被攔下接受額外檢查，之後先後三次接受CBP官員詢問。
法庭文件指出，曾偉恆在接受問詢期間的說辭不斷變化。當探員搜查他的手機時，發現了民航客機和軍用飛機的照片，以及他和其他人穿著戰術服裝、手持步槍式槍枝的照片。對此，曾偉恆辯稱這些武器是仿真氣槍。
起訴書還提到，他在第三次問詢中供稱，一名中國聯絡人指派他拍攝特定的飛機及其尾號，每張照片的報酬在20至30美元之間。他起初說自己只賺了100美元，後來又承認賺了500美元，錢匯入他的中國銀行帳戶。
他還聲稱，自己使用對方郵寄給他的SIM卡進行聯絡，每次聯絡後都會銷毀SIM卡，同時刪除聊天記錄和所拍攝的照片。
曾偉恆曾告訴海關官員，對方是透過一個「航空愛好者網站」主動聯繫他，並說這些照片會用於「研究」。不過FBI調查發現，這個網站根本不存在。他也承認，曾在2025年擅闖多倫多皮爾遜國際機場（Toronto Pearson International Airport）的聯邦快遞設施。
之後FBI接手訊問。曾偉恆宣稱，自己認為該聯絡人應該是中共的人，因為「對方開始提出更多要求後，用詞非常有條理和組織性，不像朋友之間的說話方式」。
FBI表示，曾偉恆經過進一步訊問才承認，自己與這名聯絡人發消息聯繫三個月，他說自己想幫對方是因為「覺得這很酷」，「希望有機會與特工這樣的人共事」。他還承認，對方給了他一套掩護說法，要他說自己是在拍罕見飛機。
他告訴FBI，該聯絡人希望他進一步了解美國的交通運輸與物流情況，並希望他前往奧蘭多、拉斯維加斯和洛杉磯，「獲取機場周邊特定地點的照片」。曾偉恆還聲稱，自己拒絕了這些任務，只接下奧黑爾和皮爾遜兩座機場的拍攝。
曾偉恆於8月26日被正式逮捕。他的律師團隊沒有立即回應媒體就羈押令提出的置評請求。滑鐵盧大學曾表示，不對進行中的刑事調查發表評論。

content:
在一张未注明日期的空军照片中可以看到一枚 B83 核弹。特朗普政府正在推进替代方案，现在被称为 B94。 （希尔空军基地）

华盛顿——参议院拨款委员会上周[发布](https://www.appropriations.senate.gov/news/majority/senate-appropriations-committee-releases- Five-fy-2027-funding-bills)的一份支出法案草案透露了一种名为 B94 的新核弹，专家认为这种核弹能够在引爆前深入地球深处。

B94 首先由[在线专家发现](https://x.com/armscontrolwonk/status/2121307563358839050?s=46) 确定，该名称隐藏在能源部 2027 财年支出计划中。美国能源部包括国家核安全局（NNSA），这是一个监督核武器生产和安全的半自治机构。

该委员会发布的法案草案的解释性文本 [[PDF](https://www.appropriations.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/ewd_explanatory_stmt.pdf)] 显示，在 2026 财年没有为该计划分配任何资金后，B94 的预算约为 7700 万美元。 B94 与其他正在进行的核武器计划（例如官方计划安装在即将推出的 [LGM-35A Sentinel](https://breakingdefense.com/tag/lgm-35a-sentinel/) 弹道导弹上的 W87-1 弹头）一起被列为“库存现代化”。
参议院文件没有解释这种新武器的名称，尽管军备控制专家杰弗里·刘易斯在 X 上表示，B94 很可能是先前在预算文件中确定的空射核运载系统（NDS-A）计划的新名称。刘易斯表示，B94“似乎是拜登政府[准备退役]的 B83-1 热核重力炸弹的替代品(https://breakingdefense.com/2022/10/nuclear-missile-defense-reviews-target-increasing-Russian-chinese-threats/)。

截至发稿时，参议院拨款委员会主席苏珊·柯林斯、委员会副主席帕蒂·穆雷和国家核安全局的代表尚未回应置评请求。

卡内基国际和平基金会核政策项目联席主任詹姆斯·阿克顿告诉《Breaking Defense》，B94“显然是一种新能力”，它似乎是一种空投重力炸弹，能够摧毁深埋目标。如果真是这样，阿克顿同意该武器可能会作为 B83 的替代品。

阿克顿说：“实际上，这种能力的作用将在一定程度上增加可摧毁的目标数量。”他推断，美国武器目​​前无法触及几个地下目标。

WASHINGTON — A draft spending bill [released](https://www.appropriations.senate.gov/news/majority/senate-appropriations-committee-releases-five-fy-2027-funding-bills) by the Senate Appropriations Committee last week revealed a new nuclear bomb designation known as the B94, which experts believe could be capable of penetrating deep into the earth before detonating.

The B94 was first [spotted by experts online](https://x.com/armscontrolwonk/status/2121307563358839050?s=46), who identified the designation buried in a fiscal 2027 spending plan for the Department of Energy. The DOE includes the National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA),a semi-autonomous agency that oversees the production and safety of nuclear weapons.

Explanatory text for the draft bill published by the committee [[PDF](https://www.appropriations.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/ewd_explanatory_stmt.pdf)] shows roughly $77 million budgeted for the B94, after no money was allocated for the program in FY26. The B94 is listed under “stockpile modernization” alongside other ongoing nuclear weapons programs such as the W87-1 warhead that officials plan to mount atop the forthcoming [LGM-35A Sentinel](https://breakingdefense.com/tag/lgm-35a-sentinel/) ballistic missile.

The Senate document does not explain the novel weapon name, though arms control expert Jeffrey Lewis opined on X that the B94 is likely a fresh designation for the air-launched Nuclear Delivery System (NDS-A) program previously identified in budget documents. The B94, Lewis said, “appears to be a replacement” for the B83-1 thermonuclear gravity bomb that the Biden administration [moved to retire](https://breakingdefense.com/2022/10/nuclear-missile-defense-reviews-target-increasing-russian-chinese-threats/).

Representatives for Senate Appropriations Committee Chair Susan Collins, committee Vice Chair Patty Murray and the NNSA did not respond by press time to requests for comment.

James Acton, co-director of the Nuclear Policy Program at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, told Breaking Defense the B94 is “clearly a new capability” that appears to be an air-delivered gravity bomb capable of destroying deeply buried targets. If that is the case, Acton agreed the weapon would likely serve as a replacement for the B83.

“Effectively, what this capability would be doing would be increasing somewhat the number of targets that could be destroyed,” Acton said, reasoning that several subterranean targets are currently out of reach by American weapons.

But Acton, for his part, questioned the weapon’s expected efficacy, drawing from a National Academies [report published in 2005](https://www.nationalacademies.org/read/11282/chapter/2) to argue that “once targets are below about 700 meters in depth, they’re simply not destroyable with reliability by any kind of penetrator” — though he noted that penetrating technologies have likely improved in the decades since. He stated that a higher blast yield generally helps reach more deeply buried targets, but it’s not currently clear what kind of yield the B94 may boast.

Additionally, he criticized the vacuum of information around the B94, reasoning that a new nuclear weapon deserves transparency and explanation of a larger strategy similar to what’s been promulgated by previous administrations.

“One could go on forever identifying new missions for nuclear weapons and inventing new requirements, and I view that as an essentially endless process, if not guided by some kind of broader strategy,” he said. He then raised doubts about the B94’s justification, since “there’s just going to be too many targets” it won’t be able to reach.

“I think we’re witnessing both qualitative and quantitative arms racing, and I think if the administration wants to make the case for this weapon, it should give us a clear strategy and allow us and give us enough information to really debate this capability,” he said.

特朗普訪華之際 美國封堵中國公司在東南亞租用AI算力的「後門」 - BBC News 中文
特朗普開啟亞洲之行的同時，美國商務部工業與安全局（BIS）週一（11月16日）發佈新規，要求向印尼、馬來西亞、新加坡、泰國和巴西出口、再出口或在境內轉移先進AI芯片時須申請美國許可。
新規還規定，總部或最終母公司位於中國及其他受美國武器禁運國家的企業，若通過海外數據中心租用大規模美國算力，同樣納入管制範圍。
此前，雖然美國限制最先進英偉達芯片直接銷往中國，但中國大型互聯網公司和AI實驗室可以「只租算力、不買硬件」，即芯片部署在第三國數據中心，中國企業再通過互聯網遠程調用算力訓練模型，而無須把相關硬件運入中國。
但黃仁勳不久前因媒體報道他與Megaspeed前高管黃樂存在婚外情而辭職；Megaspeed既是英偉達的合作夥伴，也因可能把受管制芯片輸往中國而受到美國當局審查。
中國外交部批評新規是「經濟脅迫」，表示北京「將採取必要措施，堅定維護自身合法權益」。
按照此前的監管框架，只要芯片沒有實際出口或再出口到中國，遠程使用算力未必直接違反美國的芯片出口管制。
這讓東南亞、日本及其他地區的大型數據中心成為中國AI研發的重要外部算力來源之一。
CNBC報道，字節跳動、阿里巴巴和騰訊等中國公司，都曾通過馬來西亞、泰國和日本等地的數據中心遠程使用英偉達芯片。
這些交易通常不會直接以中國母公司的名義簽約，而是借助離岸架構、地區子公司或本地代理商完成。
華盛頓智庫進步研究所（Institute for Progress）此前估計，到2027年，中國至少有30%的先進AI算力可能來自海外數據中心租賃及東南亞地區的芯片走私。這一比例顯示，遠程算力已經不再只是硬件禁運之外的補充渠道，而是部分中國AI公司訓練大模型的重要支柱。
圖像加註文字，黃仁勳因媒體報道他與Megaspeed前高管黃樂存在婚外情而辭職；Megaspeed既是英偉達的合作夥伴，也因可能把受管制芯片輸往中國而受到美國當局審查。
新規規定，無論數據中心位於哪個國家，只要經營實體知道或有理由知道，其客戶或客戶的最終母公司位於中國、中國澳門及其他受美國武器禁運的國家，且提供的算力達到規定門檻，相關芯片供應便須接受許可審查。
按照新規，這一門檻是「總計TPP」（即總處理性能）超過1200萬。摩根士丹利估算，這一規模約相當於700至800塊英偉達H100芯片，而訓練大型模型往往需要數千乃至上萬塊同類先進芯片。這意味著，絕大多數用於大模型訓練的海外算力集群，都會落入許可審查範圍。
不僅如此，新規還列出了五個被視為轉口風險較高的國家，即印尼、馬來西亞、新加坡、泰國和巴西。換言之，即使最終用戶並非中國企業，單純向這五個國家轉運先進芯片，同樣需要申請美國出口許可。
摩根士丹利認為，BIS正從遠程訪問、芯片出貨和代工合規三個方向同步收緊中國取得先進算力的渠道，對中國互聯網和AI產業整體偏負面。該行稱新規較其先前預期「更為鷹派」，會增加阿里巴巴的下行風險；不過，阿里旗下自研芯片公司「平頭哥」的供應能見度較高，仍可能是阿里相對同業緩解衝擊的關鍵競爭優勢。
澳洲伊迪斯科文大學（Edith Cowan University）的國際貿易專家麥克多納（Naoise McDonagh）表示，馬來西亞和泰國等國的數據中心建設高度依賴中國買家，可能受創最重。但諮詢公司Verisk Maplecroft的Reema Bhattacharya認為，新規不太可能令整個數據中心熱潮脫軌，由大型科技企業支持、客戶身份明確的投資應「保持相對韌性」。
圖像加註文字，美國商務部長盧特尼克在黃仁勳事件後收到指責，並將接受美國國會的質詢。
新規發佈之際，正值美國總統特朗普前往中國與中國國家主席習近平會晤，也發生在英偉達前首席執行官黃仁勳辭職引發的政治風波之後。黃仁勳此前因媒體報道他與Megaspeed前高管黃樂存在婚外情而辭職；Megaspeed既是英偉達的合作夥伴，也因可能把受管制芯片輸往中國而受到美國當局審查。
發佈新規的BIS，雖隸屬商務部，但在聲明中罕見地說明，新規由財政部和白宮國家安全委員會撰寫並指示發佈。
美國財政部長斯科特·貝森特（Scott Bessent）在此前表示，財政部、五角大樓、國務院和美國貿易代表辦公室數月來都支持把Megaspeed列入貿易黑名單，但掌管名單的商務部並不贊成。貝森特形容，政府內部在處理該問題時存在「不同觀點」。
美國參議院商務委員會資深民主黨成員瑪麗亞·坎特韋爾（Maria Cantwell）在11月15日寫給盧特尼克的信中表示：「如果負責保護這一優勢的機構連自己的管制措施都不執行，美國就無法保持在人工智能領域的領導地位。」她指責商務部無視反覆出現的國家安全警告，並認為盧特尼克未能行使職權，「已經損害美國國家安全」。
坎特韋爾還提到，商務部曾在調查Megaspeed期間暫停行政調查，當時司法部要求把案件移交刑事調查。她批評商務部暫停調查後，沒有同時限制Megaspeed繼續取得先進AI芯片。
她還針對特朗普政府對部分銷往中國的英偉達芯片收取25%費用的安排提出質疑，認為這可能造成批准敏感技術出口的「反常財務誘因」，並令人質疑商務部是否將商業利益置於國家安全之上。
對於黃仁勳事件，中國否認相關指控。Megaspeed也未被認定違反美國規定，該公司表示，黃樂已於2025年8月離職，公司經營合法合規，並遵守美國出口管制要求。美國商務部發言人則拒絕對坎特韋爾的信作出評論。

# LeoLabs acquires FishEye to bolster its missile defense chops

"As a wholly owned subsidiary of LeoLabs, FishEye will strengthen our ability to accelerate delivery of our next-generation radars optimized for missile warning and tracking, such as Scout-X," a LeoLabs spokesperson told Breaking Defense.

By [Theresa Hitchens](https://breakingdefense.com/author/thitchens/) on November 16, 2026 2:01 pm

WASHINGTON — Space tracking firm LeoLabs [today announced](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/leolabs-acquires-fisheye-to-accelerate-delivery-of-next-generation-radars-optimized-for-missile-warning-and-tracking-302939602.html) it has acquired FishEye Software as it looks to expand its missile defense footprint.

“As a wholly owned subsidiary of LeoLabs, FishEye will strengthen our ability to accelerate delivery of our next-generation radars optimized for missile warning and tracking, such as [Scout-X](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/09/shifting-market-sands-leolabs-moves-to-sell-new-mobile-space-radar-directly-to-allies/),” a LeoLabs spokesperson told Breaking Defense.

The highly mobile Scout-X made its debut[in June](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/06/leolabs-new-mobile-space-watch-radar-to-participate-in-valiant-shield-exercise/)during during US Indo-Pacific Command’s multinational Valiant Shield exercise. The radar fits in a standard shipping container and can detect both satellites and missiles flying at altitudes of about 230 to 1,000 kilometers (143 miles to 621 miles) above the Earth.

Founded in 1997 and headquartered in Massachusetts, FishEye has a pedigree in supporting the Pentagon’s missile defense programs. It is one of several thousand small firms chosen [last December](https://breakingdefense.com/2025/12/mda-picks-over-1000-initial-winners-for-golden-dome-contracting-vehicle/) for the Missile Defense Agency’s Scalable Homeland Innovative Enterprise Layered Defense ([SHIELD](https://breakingdefense.com/2025/08/mda-outlines-golden-domes-shield-151-billion-contracting-vehicle/))contract vehicle, which is worth up to $151 billion through 2035,and supports the Trump administration’s [Golden Dome](https://breakingdefense.com/tag/golden-dome/) initiative.

“FishEye brings decades of experience developing and integrating software for U.S. missile defense systems,” LeoLabs CEO Tony Frazier said in a statement. “That expertise will help us continue to adapt our proven radar technology for missile warning and tracking, and move those capabilities into operational use quickly.”

While the LeoLabs announcement did not reveal the price tag of the acquisition, FishEye’s revenue is projected to reach approximately $11.9 million this year, according to corporate research website [RocketReach.](https://rocketreach.co/fisheye-software-inc-profile_b5c759b1f42e0d08)

As the Nvidia scandal threatens to reignite trade tensions at Trump-Xi talks, Beijing still holds the rare earths
As the thirty-third Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Leaders’ Meeting begins this week in Shenzhen, China has set an expansive agenda, including pushing for a roadmap for Asia-Pacific-wide free trade. While many eyes are on the last-minute trilateral meeting among Chinese President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump, and Russian President Vladimir Putin this Thursday, the separate Trump and Xi bilateral, their third this year, will bring economic issues to the fore. The Nvidia scandal that broke last week has added to tensions, and semiconductor export controls loom over the trade negotiations at a moment when both Washington and Beijing have reason to preserve the truce struck in October 2025.
The smuggling of advanced US semiconductors into China, along with Chinese firms’ remote access to computing power abroad, have long concerned Washington. The Nvidia-Megaspeed controversy, in which a Singapore-based cloud provider is under investigation for allegedly diverting restricted chips to China, has further exposed potential gaps in the US export-control regime. Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing. The incident has raised questions as to whether export controls are effective in containing Chinese technological advancement and how the US can close existing loopholes. US-China trade is often shaped one economic restriction and one technical standard at a time. From outbound investment screening to various entity lists and other trade restrictions, neither side has ceased introducing new restrictions despite the trade truce, and all the while China’s April 2025 rare earth export licensing requirements remain in force.
The Chinese espionage allegations surrounding a former Megaspeed executive with reported ties to Nvidia’s Jensen Huang have already given Congress and the Department of Commerce new fuel to pursue stronger semiconductor controls. In response to Huang’s resignation as CEO of Nvidia, Representative John Moolenaar, chairman of the Select Committee on China, called on Congress to “act quickly to pass bipartisan export control legislation in the year-end national defense bill.” Current legislative efforts include the AI Overwatch Act, the Chip Security Act, and the MATCH Act, which propose measures such as requirements for chip-location verification and alignment of allied controls on semiconductor manufacturing equipment. And over the weekend, Commerce released an interim final rule to address remote access to computing power—though it is still unclear how this rule will be implemented and enforced. Tighter US restrictions on advanced chips could invite Beijing’s retaliation through stronger rare earth controls or the reinstatement of the broader restrictions whose suspension China recently extended through January 10, 2027.
In April 2025, China’s Ministry of Commerce and General Administration of Customs issued Announcement No. 18 of 2025, which implemented export controls on seven rare earth elements. While not explicitly targeted at the United States, China’s dominance of critical mineral supply chains was heavily leveraged during the trade war escalation. These export controls disrupted supply chains globally, from automakers to electronics manufacturers. As part of the Busan trade truce, the White House announced that US companies would be provided with a general license for these and other elements, describing it as a “de facto removal of controls China imposed since 2023,” but China did not make a reciprocal announcement guaranteeing access.
As shown in the chart above, US imports of selected controlled rare earth elements from China have not returned to pre–trade war levels, and US manufacturers continue to grapple with shortages of materials necessary for semiconductor production, automobiles, and national defense. International companies, including US firms, have expressed frustration over the Byzantine licensing regime, which requires extensive reporting on supply chains, while shipments remain limited even when licenses are approved.
If the US Congress capitalizes on the momentum from Nvidia’s shakeup, more semiconductor legislation could trigger tighter rare earth controls from China. Beijing could counter by reinstating its currently suspended October 2025 regulations, which would restrict transfers of Chinese-made rare-earth refining equipment and extend export controls to foreign-made products containing Chinese-origin rare earths. And despite new investments in domestic and allied critical mineral supply chains, the United States is not yet better equipped to deal with the implementation of these controls, as alternative mining and refining projects are years away from production.
The realities of long-term strategic competition could expose the limits of Trump’s personal diplomacy with Beijing and potentially jeopardize cooperation through initiatives such as the AI Safety Dialogue or the Board of Trade. China could link progress in these forums to concessions on semiconductor controls, for instance. The fallout from Nvidia is galvanizing Congress and other US agencies to intensify oversight of trade and investment with China in the next few months, and Washington will have to consider how far it can push when faced with Beijing’s rare earths chokehold.
Both Trump and Xi have reason to preserve steady relations ahead of the December Group of Twenty (G20) Leaders’ Summit in Florida, where these conversations will continue, and through the trade truce’s January expiration. But instead of tariffs and trade agreements, export controls could become the major point of contention in negotiations in 2027. While the United States cannot fully diversify its rare earth supply or rebuild a stockpile overnight, China has used its rare earth export controls since April to squeeze companies in Japan, South Korea, and the European Union as well. Diversifying supply will take long-term planning and investment. But as trade negotiations continue, Washington would benefit from a coordinated response to China’s licensing regime and its broader nonmarket practices.
Jessie Yin is an associate director at the Atlantic Council’s GeoEconomics Center.

Chinese President [Xi Jinping](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/xi-jinping/) called on Wednesday for greater international cooperation on [AI](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/artificial-intelligence/) and free trade, as pressure grows on world powers to do more to address the risks of the groundbreaking technology.

Xi made the remarks as he formally opened an [Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation](https://www.france24.com/en/asia-pacific/20261116-xi-trump-putin-discuss-world-peace-shenzhen-summit-china-says) (APEC) meeting in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen, where he is [expected to meet](https://www.france24.com/en/asia-pacific/20261114-china-to-host-first-ever-trilateral-meeting-between-trump-xi-and-putin-next-week-us-says) US President [Donald Trump](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/donald-trump/) on Thursday.

"We should actively build partnerships for scientific and technological innovation, deepen cooperation in the digital [economy](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/economy/) and artificial intelligence and promote a green and low-carbon transition," the Chinese leader said.

"By continuously transforming our innovation strengths into growth momentum, we can provide a robust impetus for economic growth in the Asia-Pacific and foster shared prosperity across the region."

Read more[China to host first-ever trilateral meeting between Trump, Xi and Putin next week](https://www.france24.com/en/asia-pacific/20261114-china-to-host-first-ever-trilateral-meeting-between-trump-xi-and-putin-next-week-us-says)

Xi also called for the elimination of trade and investment barriers, saying that it was crucial to "promote inclusive and balanced development".

He said China sought to "provide a more stable, predictable and beneficial environment for global enterprises" and would continue to expand access in its manufacturing and services sectors.

"Starting by lowering [tariffs](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/tariffs/), expanding access and exploring regulations and management standards, [China](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/china/) will conduct deep-seated reform," Xi said.

[Trade](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/trade/) tensions have been looming over the leaders of the world's two largest economies as the summit has approached.

Trump has upended the global trade order by imposing wide-ranging tariffs on many countries, which China has met head-on with counter-levies and threats to withhold crucial exports.

Read more[Xi, Trump and Putin to discuss 'world peace' at Shenzhen summit, China says](https://www.france24.com/en/asia-pacific/20261116-xi-trump-putin-discuss-world-peace-shenzhen-summit-china-says)

On the sidelines of last year's [APEC](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/apec/) summit in [South Korea](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/south-korea/), Trump and Xi reached a tenuous truce in their trade war, but it will expire in January.

content:
俄罗斯派遣两架Tu-95MS“熊”轰炸机罕见地访问越南。不同寻常的是，这架飞机似乎短暂侵入日本领空，并沿途穿过台湾防空识别区（ADIZ）。此次活动距离中国国家主席习近平、俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普将在中国深圳举行史无前例的三边会议仅48小时。一段视频的屏幕截图显示，2026 年 1 月 21 日，一架 Tu-95MS 的飞行员在前一次飞越日本海时。照片由俄罗斯国防部/阿纳多卢通过 Getty Images 拍摄 Anadolu 11 月 16 日至 17 日，Tu-95MS 轰炸机是几架俄罗斯军用飞机之一，在东北亚进行了广泛的演习，引发了三个地区政府的防空反应。据分析师 AviVector 称，共有五架涡轮螺旋桨动力轰炸机于 11 月 16 日从俄罗斯远东的乌克兰基地起飞。据报道，其中三架轰炸机在三架 Il-78M Midas 空中加油机的支援下，在日本海上空进行了大约 11 小时的训练飞行。据报道，一架 A-50U Mainstay 空中预警和控制飞机也在日本海上空飞行。与此同时，另外两架 Tu-95MS 继续向南驶向越南。今天，乌克兰空军基地的三架 Tu-95MS 和三架 Il-78M 在日本海上空进行了 11 小时的训练飞行。
一架 A-50U（RF-94268，红色 41）从符拉迪沃斯托克机场起飞，在日本海上空进行了一次侦察飞行。两架 Tu-95MS（RF-94202，红色 43；RF-94188，红色 44）… https://t.co/ezIP4s4mxl pic.twitter.com/9fvc2QZsFC — AviVector (@avivector) 11 月 17 日， 2026 日本和台湾均未正式确定参与各自空域事件的飞机类型。日本防卫省证实，11 月 17 日早些时候，两架据信是俄罗斯的飞机侵犯了福冈县冲之岛西北部的领空。第一架飞机于当地时间凌晨 4 点 07 分左右进入，于凌晨 4 点 10 分起飞。第二架飞机于凌晨 4 点 09 分左右进入，于 2026 年 4 月 10 日起飞。据日本防卫省称，凌晨 4 点 12 分，日本认为俄罗斯飞机于 11 月 17 日早些时候进入福冈附近冲之岛西北部的日本领空，第一架飞机于当地时间凌晨 4 点 07 分至 4 点 10 分左右进入日本领空，第二架飞机于当地时间凌晨 4 点 09 分至 4 点 12 分左右进入日本… https://t.co/Sj7vHUFDMQ pic.twitter.com/wYbdE7GWTH — 台湾安全监察站 (@TaiwanMonitor) 2026 年 11 月 17 日，日本防卫省称，日本航空自卫队 (JASDF) 紧急出动西方防空部队的战斗机，发出警告并采取其他措施。
穿过对马海峡后，飞机在与那国岛和台湾之间飞行，然后继续进入太平洋。 2026年11月17日，推测的俄罗斯飞机的飞行路线。 日本联合参谋部 该航线使飞机经过连接日本海、东海和西太平洋的几个具有重要战略意义的海上通道。据报道，俄罗斯飞机随后进入韩国防空识别区（KADIZ）。不过，据韩国国防部称，此次事件并未侵犯韩国领空。

Russia has sent a pair of Tu-95MS Bear bombers for a rare visit to Vietnam. Unusually, the aircraft appear to have briefly intruded into Japanese airspace and passed through Taiwan’s Air Defense Identification Zone (ADIZ) along the way. The activity unfolded just 48 hours before Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and U.S. President Donald Trump are due to hold an unprecedented trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China. A screen grab from a video shows the pilot of a Tu-95MS during a previous flight over the Sea of Japan on January 21, 2026. Photo by Russian Defense Ministry/Anadolu via Getty Images Anadolu The Tu-95MS bombers were among several Russian military aircraft conducting extensive maneuvers across Northeast Asia on November 16-17, prompting air defense responses from three regional governments. According to analyst AviVector , a total of five of the turboprop-powered bombers departed their home base of Ukrainka in Russia’s Far East on November 16. Three of the bombers reportedly conducted an approximately 11-hour training flight over the Sea of Japan, supported by three Il-78M Midas aerial refueling tankers. An A-50U Mainstay airborne early warning and control aircraft was also reported operating over the Sea of Japan. Meanwhile, the other two Tu-95MS continued south towards Vietnam. Today, three Tu-95MS and three Il-78M from Ukrainka Air Base conducted an 11-hour training flight over the Sea of Japan. An A-50U (RF-94268, 41 Red) from Vladivostok Airport conducted a reconnaissance flight over the Sea of Japan. Two Tu-95MS (RF-94202, 43 Red; RF-94188, 44… https://t.co/ezIP4s4mxl pic.twitter.com/9fvc2QZsFC — AviVector (@avivector) November 17, 2026 Neither Japan nor Taiwan officially identified the aircraft types involved in their respective airspace incidents. Japan’s Ministry of Defense confirmed that two separate aircraft believed to be Russian violated its territorial airspace northwest of Okinoshima, in Fukuoka Prefecture, early on November 17. The first aircraft entered at approximately 4:07 a.m. local time and departed at 4:10 a.m. A second aircraft entered at approximately 4:09 a.m. and departed at 4:12 a.m. Two aircraft Japan believes are Russian entered Japanese territorial airspace northwest of Okinoshima, off Fukuoka, early Nov. 17, per Japan's Ministry of Defense. The first was inside from about 4:07 to 4:10 a.m. local time and the second from about 4:09 to 4:12 a.m. The Japan… https://t.co/Sj7vHUFDMQ pic.twitter.com/wYbdE7GWTH — Taiwan Security Monitor (台灣安全觀測站) (@TaiwanMonitor) November 17, 2026 The Japan Air Self-Defense Force (JASDF) scrambled fighters from its Western Air Defense Force to issue warnings and take other measures, according to the country’s Ministry of Defense. Tokyo subsequently lodged what it described as a strong protest with Moscow over the incident. Japan also provided details of the aircraft’s subsequent route. After passing through the Tsushima Strait , the planes flew between Yonaguni Island and Taiwan before continuing into the Pacific Ocean. Flight path of the presumed Russian aircraft on November 17, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office The route placed the aircraft through several strategically important maritime approaches connecting the Sea of Japan , East China Sea , and western Pacific. The Russian aircraft then reportedly entered South Korea’s Air Defense Identification Zone (KADIZ). However, there was no violation of South Korean airspace, according to the South Korean Joint Chiefs of Staff. Finally, Taiwan’s Ministry of National Defense reported detecting two Russian military aircraft entering its ADIZ from the northeast. Overall, 2 sorties of Russian military aircraft were detected early this morning. The aircraft entered #Taiwan 's ADIZ from the northeast, flew through airspace east of Taiwan, and exited the ADIZ south of Taitung. The #ROCArmedForces have monitored the situation and responded… — 國防部 Ministry of National Defense, ROC(Taiwan) (@MoNDefense) November 17, 2026 The aircraft proceeded through airspace east of Taiwan before exiting south of Taitung. Taiwan’s armed forces monitored the activity and responded accordingly, the Ministry of National Defense said. The incident is notable because Taiwan’s defence ministry publicly identified the aircraft as Russian, rather than simply reporting unidentified military aircraft activity. As we have reported in the past , Chinese aircraft commonly fly into the southwestern part of Taiwan’s ADIZ. It is, however, worth noting that the ADIZ declared by Taiwan covers not only the entirety of the Strait but also portions of mainland China. In terms of Russian aircraft operating in Taiwan’s ADIZ, there are historical precedents, but such activity has been greatly reduced since the end of the Cold War. Taiwanese military analyst Chieh Chung told Focus Taiwan that Soviet and Russian military aircraft had previously operated inside Taiwan’s ADIZ in 1986 and January 2010. "The incident was not the first time Russian or former Soviet military aircraft had entered Taiwan's ADIZ, although such flights have become much less frequent since the end of the Cold War." https://t.co/TPUJL9hfp1 https://t.co/SDB6p3E3pD — Bryce C. Barros 白若詩 (@barros_bryce) November 17, 2026 The two remaining Tu-95MS aircraft continued south towards Vietnam and were subsequently reported at Da Nang on November 17. They were accompanied by a pair of Il-76MD Candid transports, one of which was a modernized -90A variant , to support the deployment. Tu-95MS strategic missile carriers RF-94202, RF-94188. Il-76MD, Da Nang Airport / "Danang 35K Feet". pic.twitter.com/22DaoD8PLP — Massimo Frantarelli (@MrFrantarelli) November 17, 2026 [Russie Vietnam] 2 Tu-95MS des forces aérospatiales russes sont arrivés à l'aéroport international de Da Nang (DAD/VVDN), au Vietnam. 2 avions de transport militaire IL-76 (MD et MD-90A) les accompagnaient. (c) AviaNews pic.twitter.com/4bWfFXFOik — La souris (@La_souris_DA) November 17, 2026 The flights took place against the backdrop of preparations for the November 19 meeting between Trump, Xi, and Putin in China. The summit is set to be held on the sidelines of meetings of the  Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC), which kick off tomorrow. Putin arrived in Shenzhen today. Trump has traveled first to the Philippines as part of a short tour of Asia before heading to China. Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in Shenzhen in the early hours of Nov. 18 to attend the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting. ： @PDChina pic.twitter.com/5YotpjYY6R — Shenzhen Daily (@szdaily1) November 17, 2026 The proximity of the Russian operation to the Shenzhen meeting raises questions about the strategic signaling of the Russian flights, particularly as the three governments prepare to discuss nuclear arms control, regional security, and other major international issues. The meeting is particularly unusual given the different priorities each leader is bringing to the table . Trump has indicated that he wants to discuss reducing nuclear arsenals and addressing the war in Iran. The expiration of the New START treaty in February 2026 removed the remaining bilateral limits on U.S. and Russian strategic nuclear forces, adding urgency to the question of future arms-control arrangements. U.S. President Barack Obama, at left, and Russian President Dmitry Medvedev, at right, shake hands after signing the New START treaty in 2010. Government of Russia Washington has tempered expectations of an immediate agreement, describing the gathering as an initial opportunity for the three nuclear powers to begin a conversation. Putin, meanwhile, is expected to seek discussion of Russia’s war against Ukraine and the possibility of a negotiated settlement. Moscow has signalled that Ukraine will remain a priority in its discussions with Washington. Beijing’s position is more cautious. China has resisted joining trilateral nuclear arms-control negotiations at this stage, arguing that its nuclear arsenal remains substantially smaller than those of the United States and Russia. Xi is also seeking to present China as a central diplomatic actor capable of facilitating dialogue between the other two powers. An apparent new field of Chinese intercontinental ballistic missile silos identified by Matt Korda and Hans Kristensen from the Federation of American Scientists (FAS) and located near the city of Hami in the eastern end of Xinjiang province, in the northwest of China. Kristensen/Korda/FAS 2021 The timing of the Russian aviation activity is therefore difficult to ignore. The operation demonstrated the geographic reach of Russian long-range aviation, with aircraft moving from Russia’s Far East through the approaches to Japan and Taiwan before continuing towards Vietnam. The Southeast Asian nation was a regular late Cold War operating location for Soviet naval Tu-95 Bear reconnaissance aircraft. Of course, as well as strategic signalling, flights of this kind provide valuable long-range training and intelligence collection, including assessment of regional air defense responses. The November 19 meeting may not produce an agreement on nuclear weapons or other major disputes. Still, the Russian flights underscore the fact that strategic stability in the Indo-Pacific also involves the security concerns of the regional states operating along the approaches to the western Pacific. 菲律宾马尼拉——澳大利亚和菲律宾高级官员签署了一项防务协议，以加速军事协调，为轮换部队部署和澳大利亚对菲律宾军事基础设施的投资铺平道路。 11 月 15 日签署的防务合作协议（DCA）旨在消除行政瓶颈并创建更有效的协调系统，以快速跟踪双边防务活动。到目前为止，两国的军事交流主要根据1995年的协议备忘录进行，而部队交流则以2007年签署并自2012年起生效的《访问部队地位协议》为指导。据澳大利亚国防部称，新协议涵盖情报共享、军事训练、空中和地面无人机的转让、海上活动和军事基础设施。副总理理查德·马勒斯在一份声明中表示：“这项新的防务合作安排将深化我们国防军之间的务实合作，并为共同支持地区安全创造新的机会。”菲律宾国防部长吉尔伯托·特奥多罗表示，新的 DCA 减少了官僚主义障碍，特别是在部队部署方面，并使澳大利亚能够迅速部署部队来援助菲律宾的救灾工作。特奥多罗在签约后对记者表示：“做一件事不再是 100 个步骤，而是现在只需要 10 个……而且这将更有目的性，而不是临时性的。”
此举正值澳大利亚重新调整其防御态势，以应对中国在印太地区不断扩大的军事能力、不断扩大的导弹射程以及越来越多地使用灰色地带战术和经济胁迫。菲律宾总统小费迪南德·马科斯（中）和第一夫人路易丝·阿拉内塔-马科斯（右）在 11 月 16 日于马尼拉举行的第 49 届东南亚国家联盟 (ASEAN) 峰会期间的晚宴前欢迎澳大利亚总理安东尼·阿尔巴内斯 (Anthony Albanese)。 2026 年。（Nhac Nguyen / POOL / 法新社，盖蒂图片社）“从澳大利亚的角度来看，菲律宾是我们的第一道防线，”澳大利亚战略政策研究所高级研究员尤安·格雷厄姆告诉《防务新闻》。澳大利亚遭受了解放军部队的骚扰，包括危险的海上演习、在其北部专属经济区进行激光瞄准，以及在澳大利亚皇家海军舰艇附近使用声纳和照明弹。与澳大利亚一样，菲律宾也面临着中国的压力。中国船只使用高能水炮、军用级激光，撞击和攻击菲律宾武装部队船只和人员。当被问及 DCA 是否旨在增强台湾海峡的威慑力时，特奥多罗强调该协议将增强“西菲律宾海”和“菲律宾领土”的威慑力。战略转变 澳大利亚标志着和平时期向 2023 年否认战略的历史性转变，最近将其写入 2026 年国防战略。
这个想法是将澳大利亚国防军重塑为一支一体化、集中的军队，能够威慑和阻止其进入其北部通道，其中包括部署前沿防御部队。今年早些时候，澳大利亚在总部位于布里斯班的第18保障旅下成立了新的濒海机动大队，以向更北的地区作战，使菲律宾成为该战略的重要组成部分。但分析师格雷厄姆警告称，澳大利亚只能部署小型部队。并保留这些莫

【原文 English Original】
MANILA, Philippines — Top officials from Australia and the Philippines have inked a defense pact to accelerate military coordination, paving the way for rotational troop deployment and Australian investments in Philippine military infrastructure. The Nov. 15 Defense Cooperation Agreement, or DCA, is designed to cut administrative bottlenecks and create a more efficient coordination system to fast-track bilateral defense activities. So far the two countries’ military exchanges have largely fallen under a 1995 memorandum of agreement, while troop exchanges were guided by the Status of Visiting Forces Agreement, signed in 2007 and effective since 2012. According to Australia’s Department of Defence, the new pact covers intelligence-sharing, military training, the transfer of aerial and surface drones, maritime activities, and military infrastructure. “This new Defence Cooperation Arrangement will deepen practical cooperation between our defense forces and create new opportunities to work together in support of regional security,” Deputy Prime Minister Richard Marles said in a statement. Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. said the new DCA reduces bureaucratic barriers, particularly in troop deployment, and would allow Australia to rapidly deploy troops to aid in Philippine disaster response. “Rather than 100 steps to do a single thing, it will just now take 10 … and it will be more purposeful and not ad hoc,” Teodoro told reporters following the signing. The move comes as Australia recalibrates its defense posture in response to China’s expanding military capabilities, growing missile reach, and increasing use of gray-zone tactics and economic coercion in the Indo-Pacific. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. (C) and First Lady Louise Araneta-Marcos (R) welcome Australia’s Prime Minister Anthony Albanese ahead of the Gala Dinner during the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit in Manila on Nov. 16, 2026. (Nhac Nguyen / POOL / AFP via Getty Images) “From Australia’s point of view, the Philippines is our first line of defense,” Australian Strategic Policy Institute senior fellow Euan Graham told Defense News. Australia has experienced harassment by PLA forces, including dangerous maritime maneuvers, laser targeting in its northern exclusive economic zone, and the use of sonar and flares in close proximity to Royal Australian Navy vessels. Like Australia, the Philippines faces Chinese pressure head-on. Chinese ships have used high-powered water cannons, pointed military-grade lasers, rammed, and attacked Armed Forces of the Philippines vessels and personnel. When asked if the DCA was meant to boost deterrence in the Taiwan Strait, Teodoro emphasized the agreement will bolster “deterrence in the West Philippine Sea” and in “Philippine territory.” Strategy shift Australia marked a historic peacetime shift toward a strategy of denial in 2023, most recently codified in the 2026 national defense strategy. The idea is to reshape the Australian Defense Force into an integrated, focused military capable of deterring and denying access to its northern approaches, which includes deploying a forward-defense force. Earlier this year, Australia created the new Littoral Maneuver Group under the 18th Sustainment Brigade headquartered in Brisbane, to operate farther north, making the Philippines an important part of that strategy. But Australia can only deploy small units, analyst Graham cautioned. And keeping these mobile forces supplied and operational in archipelagic countries like the Philippines is challenging, as troops and equipment are moved across widely dispersed islands during operations. Building logistics networks To that end, the new cooperation agreement is expected to facilitate discussions on potential Australian investments in Philippine military infrastructure. A list of five Luzon bases slated to receive funding for eight infrastructure projects was expected to be finalized around August this year. However, only one base has been discussed in detail so far, officials told Defense News. Teodoro previously clarified that base agreements with Australia will follow a different model than the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA) between the Philippines and the United States, which includes provisions for prepositioning military equipment and assets. The Australian “basing” arrangements, officials said, would include areas that are not traditional bases. Rather than a large basing presence, what the Australian military needs is access to locations that could sustain its forces during operations and contingencies. Discussions so far have included sustainment and logistics to support joint operations while troops spread across the archipelago’s most complex, most challenging, and remote terrains. Graham said Australia’s role in the Philippines is distinct but complementary to that of the United States. While physical locations could overlap, the infrastructure projects would be different.  Canberra and Manila in 2021 signed the Mutual Support Logistics Arrangement, which covers fuel and other supplies for aircraft and vessels, transportation, logistics, and coordination. “The importance of logistics can’t be underestimated. It’s not just about getting your fighting force fighting. You’ve got to supply them with food, fuel, and ammunition during all of that,” Graham said. More complex training With the new DCA with Australia in place, joint exercises , especially Exercise ALON, will see a larger iteration next year, Teodoro said. Exercise ALON, first held in 2023, is the biennial flagship joint training exercise between countries, focused on amphibious operations. The 2025 edition saw Australia’s largest overseas military exercise for the year and showcased the ADF projecting combat forces into the contested West Philippine Sea, Graham said. Apart from maritime training, Teodoro said there will be more aerial, land, cyber, and multidomain training exercises between Filipino and Australian troops. Military officials told Defense News that Army training has been a priority area for the Australian military’s training playbook in the Philippines. The focus follows sweeping changes in both countries’ land forces to prepare them for modern conflicts. While the Philippine Army expands from its signature jungle and urban warfare expertise toward coastal defense, the Australian ground service has pivoted toward littoral warfare. Since 2023, exchanges have focused on techniques, tactics, and procedures for amphibious operations, Army spokesperson Col. Louie Dema-ala told Defense News. But future iterations will include advanced training, Dema-ala said. “We are transitioning into a multi-domain capable Army.” The exchange is not one-sided. Australia also stands to benefit from the Philippine Army’s experience operating in dense jungle terrain. “This is not just a one-way process. We can learn from the jungle warfare fighting skills, and I think that’s important to stress. No one can tell us about the Philippines better than the Filipinos,” Graham said.

黄仁勋从公司辞职后不到一周，英伟达董事会就成立了自己的国家安全和出口管制监督委员会。根据其公告，新的常务委员会将对英伟达的“国家安全政策、出口管制合规和全球贸易风险管理”进行高层监督，其国家安全团队和全球贸易合规团队直接向该集团和临时首席执行官科莱特·克雷斯报告。深入了解 TH Premium：台湾、贸易和关税（图片来源：台积电） 虽然美国在芯片制裁上反复无常，但中国正在建立自己的芯片供应市场 中国长达十年的半导体发展状况 华为 Ascend NPU 路线图审查了中国长鑫存储的目标，到 2030 年，第六座大型晶圆厂将占据 30% 的 DRAM 内存市场份额 中国最新一轮稀土出口管制解释道英伟达董事长哈维·琼斯表示：“超级智能给国家安全带来了前所未有的挑战。” “作为全球领先的先进计算公司，Nvidia 有责任也有机会引领行业应对这些挑战。
我们致力于与政府和行业合作伙伴进行建设性合作，帮助建立和推进一个强有力的框架，利用我们掌握的一切工具来维护国家安全，同时支持持续的技术创新。”黄仁勋与被指控为中国间谍的黄爱丽丝（Alice Huang）有染的传言使该公司陷入混乱，尤其是在他承认并随后道歉之后。人们开始挖掘黄仁勋的详细信息，透露她处于错综复杂的公司网络的中心，据报道，她在将价值约 75 亿美元的被禁 Nvidia 芯片进口到中国方面发挥了重要作用。更深入的调查还显示，她的丈夫康伟是她声名鹊起的幕后黑手，并且似乎接受了她与这位亿万富翁的关系。目前尚不清楚这对夫妇做出这些精明的商业举动是否纯粹是为了利润，还是受到隐藏的第三方的控制，但这无疑使该公司面临更多审查。此后，众议院中国、外交和情报委员会主席邀请詹森参加闭门简报会，讨论英伟达的“针对外国对手间谍活动的安全协议”，而唐纳德·特朗普总统则提到联邦调查局正在调查黄仁勋与黄女士的关系。美国
2022年，美国首次对英伟达最先进的芯片A100和H100实施出口管制，迫使该公司生产符合华盛顿性能限制的中国市场A800和H800 GPU。然而，白宫在2023年再次降低了标准，导致H20的价格更加淡化，但需求量仍然很高。尽管特朗普政府没有实施拜登的人工智能扩散规则，该规则威胁要彻底禁止多个国家购买英伟达人工智能芯片，但总统最终从 2025 年 4 月至 6 月禁止向中国出口 H20 芯片。甚至在特朗普全面禁止英伟达人工智能 GPU 之前，已经有多起走私报告，一家半导体分析公司追踪了超过 1.5 吉瓦出口到中国的被禁人工智能芯片，并估计多达 150 万块英伟达 GPU 被走私。近年来走私。德斯普

Less than a week after Jensen Huang resigned from the company , Nvidia's board has created its own National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee. According to its announcement , the new standing committee will provide high-level oversight of Nvidia’s “national security policies, export control compliance, and global trade risk management,” with its National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team reporting directly to the group and to interim CEO Colette Kress. We are committed to working constructively with government and industry partners to help establish and advance a robust framework that uses every tool at our disposal to safeguard national security while supporting continued technological innovation.” The rumors of Jensen Huang’s affair with Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese spy, have thrown the company into turmoil, especially after his admission and subsequent apology . People have begun digging into details about Ms. Huang, revealing that she was at the center of a tangled web of companies and was reportedly instrumental in importing around $7.5 billion of banned Nvidia chips into China. A deeper investigation also revealed that her husband, Kang Wei, was behind her rise to prominence and seemingly accepted her relationship with the billionaire. It remains unclear if the couple made these shrewd business moves purely for profit or if they were under the control of a hidden third party, but it has certainly exposed the company to additional scrutiny. The chairpersons of the House committees on China, Foreign Affairs, and Intelligence have since invited Jensen to a closed-door briefing to discuss Nvidia’s “security protocols against foreign adversary espionage,” while President Donald Trump mentioned that the FBI is looking into Jensen Huang’s relationship with Ms. Huang. The U.S. first applied export controls to Nvidia’s most advanced chips, the A100 and H100, in 2022, forcing the company to create the China-market A800 and H800 GPUs that complied with Washington’s performance limitations. However, the White House lowered the bar once more in 2023, which resulted in the even more watered-down H20, which, nonetheless, remained in high demand. Even though the Trump administration did not implement Biden’s AI diffusion rule, which threatened to outright ban several countries from buying Nvidia AI chips, the president eventually banned the export of H20 chips to China from April to June 2025. Even before Trump’s total Nvidia AI GPU ban, there have already been multiple reports of smuggling, with one semiconductor analysis firm tracking more than 1.5 gigawatts of banned AI chips exported to China and estimating that up to 1.5 million Nvidia GPUs were smuggled in recent years. Despite that, the former Nvidia chief has always denied the allegations, saying that “ There’s no evidence of any AI chip diversion. ” Whether the allegations are true or not, it seems that the company is taking the situation seriously and taking steps to plug any leaks. As for Jensen Huang, he may be out of the company, but he still has to face Congress and all ongoing investigations.

title: UDT Australia 2026: Conference Discussions to be Catalyst for Converting Australian Debate on Undersea Warfare
zh_title: UDT Australia 2026：会议讨论将成为转变澳大利亚关于水下战争的辩论的催化剂
summary: 即将举行的首届 UDT 澳大利亚海底防御技术会议将涵盖一系列关键战略层面的问题，这些问题涉及地下领域对澳大利亚和更广泛的印度太平洋安全的影响。一位高级会议官员告诉《海军新闻》，考虑到这种影响的重要性，讨论还将证明为什么专门讨论水下活动的会议对于了解澳大利亚战略优先领域至关重要。 Clarion Defense and Security 的活动 – 将于 2026 年 12 月 2 日至 4 日在南阿德莱德的阿德莱德展览场举行
content:
即将举行的首届 UDT 澳大利亚海底防御技术会议将涵盖一系列关键战略层面的问题，这些问题涉及地下领域对澳大利亚和更广泛的印度太平洋安全的影响。一位高级会议官员告诉《海军新闻》，考虑到这种影响的重要性，讨论还将证明为什么专门讨论水下活动的会议对于了解澳大利亚战略优先领域至关重要。 Clarion Defense and Security 的活动将于 2026 年 12 月 2 日至 4 日在南澳大利亚阿德莱德阿德莱德展览场举行，将讨论“工程海底未来”这一广泛主题。它将在国际背景下解决当前和未来水下战斗空间中的全方位作战、能力、技术和工业因素。然而，对于澳大利亚来说，除了这些因素之外，也许还有一个更高的战略层面的问题，海军少将史蒂文·蒂芬（澳大利亚皇家海军退役军官，现任克拉里昂国防顾问）向《海军新闻》解释道。 “我希望实现的是认识到海底领域值得拥有自己的国家重点领域，”蒂芬少将在定义这次会议对澳大利亚国防辩论的预期影响时表示。
澳大利亚国防政策——正如最新的国防战略（2026年4月）中所规定的，并反映在国防工业发展战略（2026年7月）和海军造船和维持计划（2024年12月）中——强调了海底领域对国家利益的战略重要性。“海底能力是唯一同时作为战略、能力、主权工业、劳动力、长期投资和国际伙伴关系优先事项出现的领域。”蒂芬解释道。这位海军上将补充说，通过协调这些众多的政策要素，召开一次专门的会议来讨论该领域的不同问题并将各个利益相关者聚集在一起，将有助于“就如何实现这些优先事项达成一致”。蒂芬少将解释说，在专门论坛上对这些问题进行综合讨论可能会对澳大利亚产生更广泛的战略影响。 “澳大利亚历史上一直通过潜艇的视角来讨论海底领域。UDT Australia 寻求做的是扩大对话范围，将自主性、海底基础设施、传感、数据和通信、保障和劳动力纳入其中，”他说。
“潜艇仍然是核心，但它们现在是更大的海底事业的一部分。”这位海军上将补充道：“我希望澳大利亚 UDT 成为国家在水下领域持续努力的催化剂，因为政策信号在那里，资金在那里，需求紧迫，而且工业、国防界和国家的机会是巨大的。”澳大利亚未来的水下战输出将围绕核动力攻击潜艇（其设计如图所示）和更广泛的水下技术、系统、能力和效果建立。图片来源：澳大利亚联邦。战略原理 印度-太平洋战区正在举办一场海底竞赛，这一事实也决定了澳大利亚水下安全问题的战略意义。这体现在地区海军建造潜艇的数量、对海上关键咽喉点的海军水雷战威胁以及海底暴击的脆弱性

【原文 English Original】
The forthcoming inaugural UDT Australia undersea defence technology conference will cover a range of critical strategic-level questions relating to the impact of the sub-surface domain on Australian and wider Indo-Pacific security. Given the weight of this impact, the discussions will also demonstrate why a conference dedicated to underwater activities is vital to understanding a domain that is a strategic priority for Australia, a senior conference official told Naval News . Clarion Defence and Security’s event – taking place from 2-4 December 2026, at the Adelaide Showground, Adelaide, South Australia – will tackle the broad theme of ‘Engineering the Undersea Future’. It will address in an international context the full range of operational, capability, technological, and industrial factors featuring within the current and future underwater battlespace. However, above these factors sits perhaps a higher, strategic-level issue for Australia, Rear Admiral Steven Tiffen (a retired Royal Australian Navy officer, and now Defence Advisor at Clarion) explained to Naval News . “What I’m hoping to achieve is recognition that the undersea domain warrants its own national focus area,” Rear Adm Tiffen said, in defining the conference’s prospective impact on Australia’s defence debate. Australian defence policy – as set out in the latest National Defence Strategy (April 2026), and reflected in both the Defence Industry Development Strategy (July 2026) and the Naval Shipbuilding and Sustainment Plan (December 2024) – underscores the undersea domain’s strategic importance to national interests. “Undersea capability is the only domain that simultaneously appears as strategic, capability, sovereign industrial, workforce, long-term investment, and international partnership priorities,” Rear Adm Tiffen explained. With alignment across these numerous policy elements, holding a dedicated conference designed to discuss the domain’s different issues and draw together its various stakeholders would help generate “alignment on how to get after these priorities” , the admiral added. Such integrated discussion of the issues in a dedicated forum may have wider strategic-level impact for Australia, Rear Adm Tiffen explained. “Australia has historically discussed the undersea domain through the lens of submarines. What UDT Australia seeks to do is broaden that conversation to include autonomy; seabed infrastructure; sensing, data, and communications; sustainment; and workforce,” he said. “Submarines remain central, but they are now part of a much larger undersea enterprise.” “My hope is that UDT Australia becomes the catalyst for a sustained national effort in the undersea domain, because the policy signals are there, the money is there, the need is urgent, and the opportunities for industry, the defence community, and the country are enormous,” the admiral added. Australia’s future underwater warfare output will be built around both a nuclear-powered attack submarine (the design for which is illustrated here) and broader sub-surface technologies, systems, capabilities, and effects. Credit: Commonwealth of Australia. Strategic rationale The strategic-level significance of undersea security issues for Australia is also shaped by the fact that the Indo-Pacific theatre is hosting an undersea contest. This is manifested in the number of regional navies building submarines, naval mine warfare threats to crucial maritime chokepoints, and the vulnerability of seabed critical undersea infrastructure (CUI), Rear Adm Tiffen explained. “The Indo-Pacific is an undersea theatre – if you can’t see it, understand it, or operate consistently below the waves, you really can’t contribute to regional stability,” he said. Australia’s response to this contest is developing in both national and international contexts. In a national context, Rear Adm Tiffen said, “Australia is shifting from a balanced force to a focused force – and undersea capability is repeatedly identified as one of the most significant risk areas.” Australia’s international engagement is built largely around the AUKUS (Australia/UK/US) strategic partnership, which is encompassing delivery of a nuclear-powered attack submarine (SSN) capability for Australia (AUKUS Pillar I), plus development of various high-end, state-of-the-art underwater technologies with particular focus on autonomous systems and advanced technologies (AUKUS Pillar II). For Pillar I and the SSN capability, “[The conference will] be talking about the submarine industrial base, and we’ll examine the build [and operation] environment for the submarine force,” said Rear Adm Tiffen. These conversations will focus on the construction component, at the submarine-building yard at Osborne, South Australia, and operational elements like the sustainment enterprise underpinning the trilateral AUKUS Submarine Rotational Force – West (SRF-W, or ‘Surf West’) operations out of Perth, Western Australia. Another significant element of the conference discussions regarding Pillar I will be what to expect when Australia stands up its nuclear regulatory and safety frameworks to support an SSN capability, Rear Adm Tiffen said. For Pillar II, Rear Adm Tiffen continued, “The big question … is how do we move from the ambition we have to operational advantage? Pillar II must deliver real capability into the hands of operators.” Here, the conference will cover the specific capability and wider operational impact autonomy brings. “Autonomy is the enabler that underpins every other advanced undersea defence capability – persistent surveillance, mine countermeasures, CUI protection, and data dominance,” he explained. The admiral highlighted another crucial issue sitting across both Pillar I and Pillar II – the role of people. “Both pillars depend on how you build your workforce,” he said, adding “The undersea future will be won and lost, in my opinion, on people.” Here, it is worth noting that the naval sector’s operational, industrial, and academic communities face competition from other sectors to recruit and retain skilled workers. Consequently, workforce capacity is a defining strategic constraint on undersea capability development, Rear Adm Tiffen continued. The Royal Australian Navy (RAN) is developing and deploying autonomous capabilities, including the Ghost Shark extra-large autonomous underwater vehicle. Autonomous vehicles are arriving as part of a broadening Australian underwater enterprise. Credit: Commonwealth of Australia. Conference presence The combined importance of these various issues is illustrated by the event’s attendance levels. The collection of speakers is significant, including federal Minister for Defence and Industry Pat Conroy; plus South Australia’s premier, Peter Malinauskas, and defence and space minister Chris Picton. Speakers from the defence technology and capability community include Director General of the Australian Submarine Agency, Vice Admiral Jonathan Mead; Chief Defence Scientist, Professor Tanya Munro; and Head of the defence department’s Advanced Strategic Capabilities Accelerator (ASCA) programme, Major General Hugh Meggitt. ASCA’s role is worth highlighting, as the organisation that places investments in innovations designed for accelerated capability delivery to the warfighter, Rear Adm Tiffen explained. The 11 countries present for UDT Australia include all three AUKUS partners, alongside France and Japan as two other countries bringing significant naval output in the region. Other prominent conference statistics include 85 industry organisations and around 40 industry exhibitors being present (the latter showcasing technologies including autonomy, sensors, propulsion, communications, sustainment, and advanced materials). Given the regional significance of the AUKUS build-work in South Australia and operational output in Western Australia, the Defence South Australia and Defence West government agencies are also present. Within an overall attendance aim of around 1,500 – 2,000 people, the science and technology and academic research communities are strongly represented too. In sum, Rear Adm Tiffen said, the conference attendance is quite diverse for an inaugural event. Here, he noted the importance too of people and stakeholders making connections and building networks across the assembled attendees, adding “I’m amazed by the power of networks to move the needle on really thorny issues …. The real thing I’m looking for is people making those connections and realizing they might have solutions for the problems some have already identified.” Industrial deterrence With the conference presenting an opportunity to build integrated discussion around the importance of the undersea domain as a defence and wider national security priority, Rear Adm Tiffen reinforced the role of industry – not only in this conversation, but in building the capability resilience needed to underpin that national defence requirement. With policy aligned and funding committed, delivering capability is the next step. Here, Rear Adm Tiffen explained, industry can play a fundamental role in supporting national defence requirements and wider national interests, through contributing to the delivery of deterrence. “In Australia, we made industry a fundamental input into capability,” he said. “If you take that to an extreme, how do you get industry to be part of your deterrence?” “In this context, deterrence is not just platforms and weapons, but the ability to repair, replenish, sustain, and regenerate capability at scale,” the admiral continued. This means interweaving industrial infrastructure, capacity, and output into the fabric of national resilience to the point that any adversary will treat that overall industrial capability with greater respect, Rear Adm Tiffen explained. Building such industrial resilience is central to underpinning industry’s ability to become a national-level deterrent component. Constructing capability to deter threats in the underwater domain is, after all, one of the priority strategic messages the UDT Australia conference is looking to convey. Naval News comment Clarion’s UDT Europe conference has in very recent years become a focal point for governments, navies, industry, and the academic community to engage on underwater threats in the North Atlantic, particularly because the high-level risk from Russian SSN operations and lower-level risk from rogue shipping to CUI has put underwater warfare firmly in the political and public spotlight. In Australia, challenges to underwater security, plus programmes like AUKUS, have already put the undersea domain in the same spotlight. The UDT Australia conference presents an opportunity to generate an integrated debate on how to address these challenges from strategic, operational, capability, technological, industrial, and people perspectives. title: MANGROVE completes first phase of NATO underwater battlespace network, eyes Arctic trial
zh_title: MANGROVE完成北约水下作战空间网络第一阶段，着眼于北极试验
summary: Saab 领导的 MANGROVE 联盟已经完成了北约盟军水下作战空间任务网络 (AUWB-MN) 计划的第一阶段，提供了一个参考架构，该联盟目前计划在 2027 年 7 月的北极 X 特遣队演习期间将其带入海上。北约反潜战 (ASW) 屏障智能防御计划项目主任戴维·伯顿 (David Burton) 在 11 月 16 日向媒体通报情况时表示，北约盟军指挥转型(ACT) 已授权 AUWB-MN 作为此次演习的“选择架构”，演习将在高北地区进行，地点尚未确定。
content:
Saab 领导的 MANGROVE 联盟已经完成了北约盟军水下作战空间任务网络 (AUWB-MN) 计划的第一阶段，提供了一个参考架构，该联盟目前计划在 2027 年 7 月的北极 X 特遣队演习期间将其带入海上。北约反潜战 (ASW) 屏障智能防御计划项目主任戴维·伯顿 (David Burton) 在 11 月 16 日向媒体通报情况时表示，北约盟军指挥转型(ACT) 已授权 AUWB-MN 作为此次演习的“选择架构”，演习将在高北地区进行，地点尚未确定。 AUWB-MN 旨在提供一个包含标准、协议和安全原则的通用架构框架，使盟军海军能够共享数据并作为一支综合力量操作有人和无人系统，无论每个国家使用什么技术或系统。伯顿将这一概念比作“水下互联网”，旨在满足随着海军从运营数量相对较少的大型平台过渡到运营数百或数千个小型无人资产而日益增长的互操作性需求。 “目前，我们还没有定义的互联网——标准和协议的架构，”他说。他警告说，如果没有共同的架构，各国就有可能开发出独立的、不兼容的系统，这将阻止北约充分利用其集体资产的能力。
通用架构 第一阶段的输出——超过 600 页的参考架构报告和随附的软件模型——已于 2026 年 9 月底提交给北约，目前正在由 12 个赞助国进行审查。这项工作的重点不是创建新标准，而是将与海事行动相关的许多现有北约标准化协议 (STANAG) 整合到一个单一的、连贯的架构中。伯顿表示，该架构与供应商无关，并且没有规定具体的技术解决方案。 “参考架构是一个逻辑架构。它不规定解决方案，”他说。 “因此，这使各国有机会获得自己的解决方案，前提是它们满足参考架构的限制。” MANGROVE联盟于2025年7月被北约选中，并于当年9月1日正式开始工作。该计划是北约数字海洋计划和英国领导的反潜战屏障智能防御计划的一部分，由英国领导的 12 个赞助国资助。该联盟由 Saab 海军业务领域牵头，还包括 CETENA 和 Fincantieri Group 的 IDS、FlySight、GraalTech、Miraya、Saab UK、S2IX 和普利茅斯大学。
英国萨博海军业务发展主管、MANGROVE联盟联合主席克里斯·拉德对媒体表示，第一阶段工作的规模不容小觑，该联盟必须在12个月内建立多国工作结构，与赞助国协调，并确定和协调相关的北约标准。我们已经取得了巨大的进步，”他说。从架构到测试 第一阶段大约 80% 的工作重点是开发参考架构，其余 20% 为测试和参考环境 (TRE) 奠定基础，这将是下一阶段的主要重点。 TRE 将提供一种评估新传感器、平台和其他系统是否符合架构互操作性要求的方法。

【原文 English Original】
The Saab-led MANGROVE consortium has concluded the first phase of NATO’s Allied Underwater Battlespace Mission Network (AUWB-MN) programme, delivering a reference architecture that the alliance is now planning to take to sea during its Task Force X Arctic exercise in July 2027. Briefing media on 16 November, David Burton, project director of the NATO Anti-Submarine Warfare (ASW) Barrier Smart Defence Initiative, said NATO’s Allied Command Transformation (ACT) had mandated the AUWB-MN as the “architecture of choice” for the exercise, which will take place in the High North at a location yet to be confirmed . The AUWB-MN is intended to provide a common architectural framework incorporating standards, protocols and security principles that will enable allied navies to share data and operate crewed and uncrewed systems as an integrated force, regardless of the technology or systems each nation uses . Burton likened the concept to an “underwater internet”, designed to address the growing need for interoperability as navies transition from operating relatively small numbers of large platforms to potentially hundreds or thousands of smaller, uncrewed assets . “At the moment, we haven’t got that defined internet – that architecture of standards and protocols,” he said. Without a common architecture, he warned, nations risk developing separate, incompatible systems that will prevent NATO from fully exploiting the capabilities of its collective assets. Common architecture The Phase 1 output – a reference architecture report of more than 600 pages and an accompanying software model – was submitted to NATO at the end of September 2026 and is now being reviewed by the 12 sponsor nations . Rather than creating new standards, the work has focused on bringing together the many existing NATO standardisation agreements (STANAGs) relevant to maritime operations within a single, coherent architecture . Burton said the architecture is vendor-agnostic and does not prescribe specific technological solutions. “The reference architecture is a logical architecture. It doesn’t stipulate solutions,” he said. “So, this gives nations the opportunity to acquire their own solutions, providing they meet the limits of the reference architecture.” The MANGROVE consortium was selected by NATO in July 2025 and formally began work on 1 September that year . The programme forms part of NATO’s Digital Ocean initiative and the UK-led ASW Barrier Smart Defence Initiative and is funded by 12 sponsor nations led by the UK. Led by Saab’s Naval business area, the consortium also includes CETENA and IDS of the Fincantieri Group, FlySight, GraalTech, Miraya, Saab UK, S2IX and the University of Plymouth . Chris Lade, head of naval business development at Saab UK and co-chair of the MANGROVE consortium, told media that the scale of the Phase 1 undertaking should not be underestimated, with the consortium having to establish a multinational working structure, co-ordinate with the sponsor nations and identify and reconcile relevant NATO standards within 12 months. “ We’ve come a huge way,” he said. From architecture to testing Around 80% of the Phase 1 effort was focused on developing the reference architecture, with the remaining 20% laying the foundations for a test and reference environment (TRE) that will be a principal focus of the next phase . The TRE will provide a means of assessing whether new sensors, platforms and other systems comply with the architecture’s interoperability requirements before they are introduced into multinational operations . According to Lade, a system developer will be able to connect a new system or sensor to the TRE and receive an assessment identifying whether it meets the required standards or where modifications are needed . In parallel with preparations for the next phase, the consortium is working with NATO’s Centre for Maritime Research and Experimentation (CMRE) in La Spezia, Italy, to apply the architecture during Task Force X Arctic in July 2027 . Lade said the intention is to demonstrate the architecture during at least part of the exercise, although commercial arrangements with NATO are still being worked through . The exercise will provide an early opportunity to assess how the architecture can support interoperability between different systems in a live maritime environment . Next phase Phase 1 was funded with EUR 1 million contributed by the 12 sponsor nations, with the nine consortium members also contributing financially to its completion . With no immediate follow-on contract in place, the Phase 1 contract has been extended by 12 months to maintain momentum and support interim activities, including preparations for Task Force X Arctic . Funding arrangements for this bridging work are still being finalised . Separately, EUR 1 million has been secured from NATO for an initial follow-on phase, known as Spiral Zero, which is expected to begin in early 2027 . Lade said he anticipated that the full Phase 2 programme, which will focus on developing the TRE and further refining the architecture, will begin around mid-2027 . Wider adoption Alongside preparations for Phase 2, work is also under way to assess how the AUWB-MN architecture aligns with existing and planned national capabilities . Lade said the UK has already undertaken an independent comparison between MANGROVE and the network architecture being developed under its Atlantic Bastion initiative, finding “not very much delta at all” . Canada is conducting a similar assessment, and bilateral discussions with the sponsor nations are planned for December to identify any areas requiring adjustment. Meanwhile, additional countries have expressed interest in joining the programme . Finland has indicated its intention to participate, Greece has shown interest, and discussions are under way with Belgium and France . For Burton, the broader objective is to ensure that NATO and its partners converge on a common approach rather than develop competing national or regional solutions . “We don’t want multiple architectures,” “Whether we’re talking about the UK, whether we’re talking about Europe, whether we’re talking about AUKUS, we want one architecture.” David Burton, project director of the NATO Anti-Submarine Warfare (ASW) Barrier Smart Defence Initiative The post MANGROVE completes first phase of NATO underwater battlespace network, eyes Arctic trial appeared first on Naval News .

title: ‘Davidson Window’ Admiral Hopes He Was Wrong On China’s Ability To Take Taiwan By 2027
