summary: 五年前，这位在国会作证的人提出了所谓的“戴维森窗口”，即中国有能力在 2027 年之前对台湾发动可信的入侵，现在这个日期即将到来，他为他的想法提供了一些见解。当时在太平洋地区指挥美军的海军上将菲利普·戴维森 (Philip Davidson) 在周五发布的播客中表示，自他 2021 年退役以来发生的一些事态发展可能会改变他的预测。然而，美国印太司令部（现太平洋司令部或PACOM）前司令告诉我们为什么要关心这个问题
content:
五年前，这位在国会作证的人提出了所谓的“戴维森窗口”，即中国有能力在 2027 年之前对台湾发动可信的入侵，现在这个日期即将到来，他为他的想法提供了一些见解。当时在太平洋地区指挥美军的海军上将菲利普·戴维森 (Philip Davidson) 在周五发布的播客中表示，自他 2021 年退役以来发生的一些事态发展可能会改变他的预测。然而，美国印太司令部（现太平洋司令部或PACOM）前司令告诉《我们为什么要关心印太？》他仍然认为有理由担心。他特别敦促美国在入侵台湾之前向台湾提供军事援助，以更好地威慑中国采取行动。中国军队练习海滩登陆。 (解放军) 戴维森发表上述声明之际，中国一直在稳步增加在台湾周边的军事演习，中国认为台湾是一个分裂的省份，有朝一日将重新置于其控制之下。在了解戴维森对 SeaLight 基金会创始人兼执行董事雷·鲍威尔 (Ray Powell) 和 BowerGroupAsia 高级顾问吉姆·卡鲁索 (Jim Carouso) 所说的话之前，让我们回顾一下戴维森于 2021 年 3 月 9 日对参议院军事委员会所说的话。
戴维森在谈到中国​​时表示：“我担心他们正在加速实现取代美国的野心，以及我们在基于规则的国际秩序中发挥领导作用的野心，他们长期以来一直表示希望在 2050 年之前实现这一目标，我担心他们会进一步接近这一目标。”菲利普·戴维森，当时担任海军上将和美国印度太平洋司令部司令。 （美国海军）两年后，对所谓“戴维森之窗”的评估得到了中央情报局（CIA）的支持。时任中央情报局局长比尔·伯恩斯 (Bill Burns) 表示：“习主席已指示中国军事领导层解放军 (PLA) 在 2027 年之前做好入侵台湾的准备。”从那以后发生了什么变化？ “从本质上讲，我希望我是错的，”戴维森在谈到他的国会证词时说道。 “如果我错了，那就意味着我们向印太司令部建议的事情、美国政府和其他国家政府在过去七年里采取的事情是有效的。而且没有发生战争。” “我主张，从军事意义上来说，五套能力——我认为很重要的投资指南，”戴维森解释道，他现在是国防承包商 AV 的董事会成员。
“美国需要重新考虑其在印太地区的兵力态势和设计——我们在哪里、我们如何部署、我们轮换什么、这些部队的能力是什么。我们还需要更多样化、更大规模的联合部队火力，这意味着进攻性火力不仅来自海上，还来自陆地和空中。”这位海军上将补充道：“你现在肯定会看到这种情况正在发生，包括部署和导弹部署、海军陆战队、陆军在菲律宾和第一岛链沿线的部署。” “这很有帮助。”第 1 多域特遣部队远程火力营第 3 野战炮兵团第 5 营查理炮台的中程能力 (MRC) 发射器抵达菲律宾吕宋岛北部战区，这是该能力首次部署到战区的一部分

【原文 English Original】
The man whose congressional testimony five years ago led to what’s known as the “Davidson Window” for China being capable of launching a credible invasion of Taiwan by 2027 is offering some insights into what he is thinking now that the date is drawing near. Philip Davidson – the admiral who led U.S. forces in the Pacific at the time – said on a podcast released Friday that several developments have taken place since he retired in 2021 that could change his projection. However, the former commander of U.S. Indo-Pacific Command (now Pacific Command or PACOM) told the Why Should We Care About the Indo-Pacific? podcast he still sees reasons for concern. In particular, he urged the U.S. to deliver military aid to Taiwan before an invasion to better deter China from acting. Chinese forces practice a beach landing. (PLA) Davidson’s statements were delivered as China has been steadily increasing military exercises around Taiwan , which it considers a breakaway province that it will someday bring back under its control. Before getting into what Davidson told podcasters Ray Powell, founder and executive director of the SeaLight Foundation , and Jim Carouso, a senior advisor at BowerGroupAsia , let’s recall what Davidson told the Senate Armed Services Committee on March 9, 2021. “I worry that they are accelerating their ambitions to supplant the United States, and our leadership role in the rules-based international order, which they have long said that they want to do that by 2050, I am worried about them moving that target closer,” Davidson said of China. “Taiwan is clearly one of their ambitions before then, and I think the threat is manifest during this decade, in fact, in the next six years.” Philip Davidson when he was a Navy admiral and commander of U.S. Indo-Pacific Command. (USN) The assessment of the so-called “Davidson Window” was backed two years later by the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA). “President Xi has instructed the PLA [People’s Liberation Army], the Chinese military leadership, to be ready by 2027 to invade Taiwan,” then-CIA Director Bill Burns stated . What’s Changed Since Then? “At the heart of it, I’m hoping to be wrong,” said Davidson about his congressional testimony. “If I’m wrong, that means the things we recommended from Indo-Pacific Command, the things that the United States government and other governments have undertaken over the last seven years, have been effective. And there hasn’t been war.” “I advocated for, just in the military sense, five capability sets – investment guidelines that I thought were important to do,” explained Davidson, now on the board of directors at defense contractor AV . “The United States needed to rethink its force posture and design in the region, in the Indo-Pacific – where we are, how we deployed, what we rotated through, what the capabilities of those sets were. We also needed more diverse and a larger set of joint force fires, meaning offensive fires, not just from the sea, but from land and air domain.” “You’re certainly seeing that play out right now, with deployments and missile deployments, with Marine formations , Army formations in the Philippines and along the First Island Chain,” the admiral added. “That has been a help.” Mid-Range Capability (MRC) Launcher from Charlie Battery, 5th Battalion, 3rd Field Artillery Regiment, Long Range Fires Battalion, 1st Multi-Domain Task Force arrives as part of the capability’s first deployment into theater on Northern Luzon, Philippines, April 8, 2024. The MRC deployment aims to enhance Philippine maritime defense capabilities, while bolstering interoperability and readiness within the U.S.-Philippine Alliance. (U.S. Army) U.S. Army In addition, Davidson noted that the U.S. “needed to improve our exercises, our experimentation, and our innovation in the region. We have deepened the relationship with Japan and Australia in the Keen series of exercises over the last five years, and in a way that was kind of unheard of in my day, which I think is a profound improvement.” The Keen Sword training exercise occurred last month and saw about “45,000 Japan Self-Defense Force, 11,000 U.S. service members and forces from Australia, Canada, France, Germany, the Netherlands, New Zealand and the Philippines…participating alongside observers from the Republic of Korea and the United Kingdom,” according to the U.S. Navy. A Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force Landing Craft Air Cushion (LCAC) hovercraft assigned to Amphibious Warfare Squadron One, Amphibious and Mine Warfare Group, coasts into the harbor at Marine Corps Air Station Iwakuni, Japan, Oct. 28, 2026, during Keen Sword. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Lance Cpl. Donald Dugger) Lance Cpl. Donald Dugger Japan taking a more assertive security posture toward China has been a huge change from when he was in command, Davidson noted. “Japan absolutely has come forward, they reissued their national security strategy in December of [2022], and there were a number of alliance announcements made in January of [2023],” he explained.  The Japanese doubled their investment in defense from 1% to 2% of its GDP, Davidson highlighted. Japan also “established space [and] cyber forces, instilled the cybersecurity principles and laws that would be necessary to deepen our relationship in a classified way. And this is almost unknown to anybody in America. Completely redistributed and reset their ground formations and air formations in the Southwest Island chain, between Okinawa and along the Ryukyu chain.” “Most importantly, they identified China as the strategic threat in the region,” Davidson proffered. “And in the alliance announcement in January of [2023] with us, said that our interests have converged in this regard.” A Japan Air Self-Defense Force F-15 fighter performs during the Komatsu Air Festival on September 26, 2026 in Komatsu, Japan. (Photo by Zhang Hui/VCG via Getty Images) VCG Taiwan too has made some needed improvements in its approach to defending itself since he retired, Davidson explained. “You have to be encouraged by Taiwan’s actions taken since then,” he stated. “They expanded the conscription timeline from just a few months to a year of service. They have done an enormous amount of work in their national emergency preparedness realm.” Davidson also credited Adm. Lee Hsi-min, chief of the Taiwanese Armed Forces general staff from 2017 to 2019, for developing the Overall Defense Concept (ODC). Lee envisioned a mix of mines, uncrewed aerial systems (UAS), uncrewed surface vehicles (USVs), uncrewed underwater vehicles (UUVs), crewed coastal defense boats, land-based mobile short- and medium-range precision munitions, precision-guided multiple launch rocket systems, man portable air defense systems (MANPADS), anti-armor rocket systems and electronic warfare measures to counter the PLA’s overwhelming advantages in aviation and naval assets and long-range fires. Taiwan sits about 130 miles east of China. (Google Earth) “He said, ‘We really have to develop the kind of asymmetric capabilities that help round out our lack of capacity vis-a-vis its relationship with the People’s Republic of China, and make sure that we have a strategic and operational design that can kill in the littoral and along the landing beaches and things like that,’” Davidson pointed out. “They’ve been getting after autonomy. They’ve been getting after robotics and drones and sensing.” In 2025, Taiwan revealed a new drone boat, or uncrewed surface vessel (USV), the Endeavor Manta, said to be the first of its kind for the Republic of China Navy (ROCN). However, as we have frequently pointed out , Taiwan is still far behind where it needs to be in many of these areas, but especially uncrewed systems . In addition, Davidson said growing relations with the Philippines and Australia are also helping. Australia signed the Australia–United Kingdom–United States security partnership (AUKUS) in September 2021, months after Davidson retired. AUKUS calls for the United States and Britain to share nuclear-submarine technology with Australia. A rendering of the future SSN-AUKUS design. (U.K. Ministry of Defense) “So over the span of the last six years since March 9 of 2021, you’ve seen a lot of change that I think has reinforced the deterrence of the West here, and I think that’s important to note,” Davidson stated. What Still Needs To Change Despite seeing the U.S. and its allies better prepared to defend against a Chinese invasion of Taiwan, Davidson said he is concerned that the U.S. is not moving fast enough to provide promised military aid. “I would like to see the $14 billion in committed [Foreign Military Sales] to Taiwan move over there in the next few months or a year,” Davidson stated. Approval of the package, which is a major point of controversy with China, has been stalled, Taiwan’s Defense Minister Wellington Koo said in September . The minister’s remarks “come as concerns mount that President Donald Trump could halt arms sales to Taiwan. China has pressed Washington to halt the arms sales, most prominently during a May summit in Beijing between Trump and China’s President Xi Jinping,” The Associated Press noted . “The United States paused the $14 billion arms deal after that meeting.” The package “largely consists of [Patriot] PAC-3 and NASAMS [ National Advanced Surface-to-Air Missile System ] air defense missiles,” Reuters reported . However, another huge factor beyond tensions with China is the U.S. supply of these air defense munitions, which has been drastically affected by the current and recent Middle East conflicts . Donations to Ukraine have also eaten into U.S. stocks. The lack of sufficient magazine depth is an issue that TWZ has raised frequently for years, and especially in regard to America’s air and missile defenses , in particular. Commitments for deliveries to 20 other nations and an overall insatiable global demand for interceptors due to numerous destabilizing events has put further strain on the supply of American interceptors. All this is also straining the ability of industry to provide enough capacity. For instance, current PAC-3 MSE production “is around the baseline rate of 650 interceptors per year, with half the deliveries going to the United States and the rest to allies and partners,” according to a report from the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS). The Pentagon is trying to boost production. Under a contract with the Pentagon inked in January , Lockheed Martin is committed to raising annual Patriot output to 2,000 interceptors. A Patriot PAC-3 interceptor (Lockheed Martin) In addition to wanting to see the arms package pushed forward, Davidson warned about China’s information warfare capabilities. “The one thing that has really jumped out at me that was a problem, certainly, when I was the Indo-Pacific commander, but it’s worse now, is the information environment,” Davidson posited. “China is working to undermine the democratic processes in Taiwan. They’re working to undermine any U.S. citizens’ confidence in business leadership and political leadership and military leadership. They’re exploiting accidents or difficulties that someone might be having to flood social networks, and it’s happening not just from China, but from Russia and Iran and independent actors elsewhere. “ “It’s really dangerous,” the former commander emphasized. “There’s been some estimations that some of the activity from bots and from propaganda players is accounting for up to 70% of the commentary in social media threads here and there, and that’s a much more difficult place to be.” Davidson said the U.S. needs to step up its own information warfare capabilities. “I think we should be putting as much effort into [the information domain] as we’ve been putting into drones and autonomy and things like that in this day and age,” Davidson stated. Chinese hovercraft land on a beach during training. (PLAN) Davidson did not address some other glaring issues in regard to China’s potential seizure of Taiwan. The biggest being will the U.S. actually respond militarily if a major Chinese exercise suddenly became an actual invasion operation? Would there even be enough time and what about China’s anti-access capabilities that could keep much of America’s combat power at bay during the early stages of such a conflict? Would there even be support for such an intervention operation domestically, especially considering it could be very bloody and it would surely manifest itself here at home? Then, as we mentioned in the piece, there are many areas where Taiwan seems to be moving far too slowly while China’s military force continues to balloon on nearly all fronts. Regardless, it’s nice to hear from the man who inadvertently gave birth to the “Davidson Window” now that this ominous window of vulnerability he predicted a half decade is cracking open. As the Pentagon finalizes its review of U.S. force posture in Europe, one relatively small commitment deserves protection from the budget axe: the roughly 600 American troops serving in NATO’s Kosovo Force. They barely register in a debate about brigades and billion-dollar line items, but they keep a hard-won peace in the Balkans, and pulling them out would save almost nothing while handing Moscow a cheap strategic win. KFOR was deployed in June 1999 under NATO command, after the alliance bombed Yugoslavia to stop the violence perpetrated by Slobodan Milosevic’s Serbian forces against ethnic Albanians. Kosovo declared independence in 2008, but Serbia, backed by Russia and China, still refuses to recognize it. The Europe posture review is a legitimate exercise. After years of urging European allies to shoulder more of their own conventional defense, the Trump administration is right to ask hard questions about where American forces add unique value and where Europe can step up given suitable time to develop their capabilities and capacities. But KFOR is a mission in which the American role is not easily replaced, because it is as much political as military, and where a wrong call risks instability on Europe’s southeastern flank. Start with the threat. Even while absorbing heavy losses in Ukraine, Vladimir Putin has not given up on destabilizing Europe. The Balkans, Europe’s soft underbelly, are a favored arena: cheap to stir, a place to distract Western attention from Ukraine. Moscow has long used Serbia as a lever against Kosovo’s stability. In 2017, a Russian-made train was sent toward northern Kosovo, a rolling provocation that bore the slogan “Kosovo is Serbia.” Russia runs a so-called humanitarian center near Kosovo that is suspected of serving as a Russian intelligence station. Close Serbian-Russian intelligence ties give Moscow access to local nationalist forces prepared for provocations. In 2023, an armed attack on Kosovo police in the north, which Pristina blamed on Serbian-backed militants, heightened fears that Russian-aligned actors were exploiting the tension; earlier that year, Russia’s Minister of Foreign Affairs warned that “a major explosive situation is brewing in the heart of Europe.” Tensions have repeatedly flared. In May 2023, clashes between Serb protesters and Kosovo police injured more than 90 NATO peacekeepers and prompted Serbia to raise its military alert level. That September, an attack in Banjska, where heavily armed Serb gunmen killed a Kosovo police officer and barricaded themselves in a monastery, showed how quickly a local flare-up can become a regional crisis. The danger has not passed. Serbian strongman Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat in Serbia’s Oct. 25 parliamentary election, but Belgrade’s foreign-policy direction is uncertain and there are concerns that its views on Kosovo will not change. In October, Russia’s ambassador to the UN warned that the situation in Kosovo “remains persistently tense and is literally teetering on the brink.” Still, Kosovo and Serbia have remained at peace since 1999, in large part because of KFOR. In the words of a bipartisan group of U.S lawmakers, the force functions as “a political deterrent to those seeking to stoke ethnic violence.” An American drawdown from KFOR may embolden nationalist agendas in Kosovo and Serbia as well as separatist ambitions in Republika Srpska, the Serb-dominated region in nearby Bosnia. The American presence in KFOR is valued precisely because it is American. U.S. troops have anchored KFOR since its creation, and Washington currently leads Regional Command East, a position of real operational weight, not symbolism. The U.S. has traditionally provided the 600 or so American troops—often Army National Guardsmen—an economy-of-force mission with minimal cost or effect on the U.S. Army’s ability to execute missions elsewhere around the globe. The mission accounts for less than 1 percent of the total U.S. troops in Europe. KFOR’s value becomes plain when contrasted with Operation Althea in neighboring Bosnia. EUFOR, an EU-led force with roughly 1,500 troops, has struggled to respond decisively to repeated provocations by Republika Srpska leader Milorad Dodik, who’s backed by Moscow and Belgrade. EU ambassadors rejected Bosnian appeals to help enforce an arrest warrant against him in 2025, citing political risk. Dodik has openly mocked EUFOR’s patrols. Lacking an American anchor and a unified chain of command willing to act, EUFOR has too often had to manage crises rather than deterring them. KFOR, by contrast, has demonstrated it can surge forces when tested, providing genuine deterrence. After the 2023 Banjska incident, NATO increased its peacekeeping presence in Kosovo. Serbia drew down its border deployment, ending the crisis. The Pentagon is right to ask what the value of an American military presence is worth. For KFOR, the answer is plain: a few hundred U.S. troops are successfully maintaining a quarter-century-long peace that Russia would love to see unravel. Lawmakers from both parties already understand that. The Pentagon should, too, and keep KFOR intact. Mark Montgomery, a retired U.S. Navy rear admiral, serves as a senior director at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies’ (FDD), where Ivana Stradner is a research fellow. ]]>

【原文 English Original】
TWZ has obtained new details about the ongoing repairs to the Seawolf class submarine USS Connecticut following collision with an underwater seamount in the South China Sea in 2021. The Navy had been looking at a roughly three-year timeline for the construction of a replacement bow sonar dome. In the end, it took just under a year for it to be built. The overall schedule for repairs to Connecticut has suffered delays, and we were the first to report that the boat is now not expected to return to service until next summer. Editor’s note: After this story was published, Janicki Industries reached out to us to ask that the image of the dome be taken down while an additional review is conducted. Out of courtesy, we agreed, and we will repost it if and when it is fully approved. Janicki Industries produced the new bow sonar dome in approximately 10 months and delivered it to the Navy in 2024, the company told us today. Janicki has a history of producing “sonar domes and precision machined hardware” for U.S. nuclear submarine programs, according to its website . It has also supported various high-profile aerospace programs, including the B-21 Raider bomber and F-35 Joint Strike Fighter . Connecticut ’s bow had initially remained attached, at least to some degree, following the collision five years ago, according to a heavily redacted Navy report on the accident . However, the entire bow structure subsequently broke away as the submarine limped to Guam . The boat then sailed to San Diego, California , and then to the Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS-IMF) in Washington State, where it has been ever since. USS Connecticut seen at the Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & Intermediate Maintenance Facility in 2023 with its bow dome prominently missing. USN “Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & IMF [Intermediate Maintenance Facility] needed a precision replacement dome with no production line behind it, on the boat’s schedule,” Janicki also says on its website at the time of writing . “Janicki delivered it 24 months faster than the next-best option because everything the job needed sits under one roof: 5-axis mills that fit a hemisphere, the metrology to prove it, and the 1,000-ton press that forms double-curved plate.” The picture seen in part at the top of this story and in full below shows one of Janicki’s proprietary five-axis milling machines at work on the dome. The size and complexity of the bow sonar dome on Seawolf class submarines cannot be overstated. The bow sonar arrays on these boats is 24 feet in diameter. The structure of the dome itself has to be built to very exacting specifications for the sonar system to work properly. A look at the bow sonar array on a Seawolf class submarine with its bow dome removed. Public Domain Past Pentagon budget documents and appropriations bills from Congress had already highlighted the expected costs and complexities of replacing Connecticut ’s bow sonar dome. In 2021, lawmakers approved $10 million in funding specifically for the dome, as well as $40 million for other “emergent repairs.” The full repair bill is still unknown, but is expected to be far steeper than just $50 million. In its Fiscal Year 2025 budget proposal , released in 2024, the Navy also outlined plans to acquire an additional bow dome in case any of its Seawolf class submarines suffered another similarly severe mishap. “The Seawolf Class submarines sustainment strategy did not include the provisioning of replacement bow domes; therefore, no replacement bow domes for these in-service submarines are within the Navy’s inventory,” the budget documents explained. “This program would procure one Seawolf Class bow dome for use in the event replacement is required. Funds in FY25 are to purchase a bow dome which has a three plus year lead time.” Note here the mention of a lead time of at least three years, which is in line with Janicki’s statement that the “next-best option” would have taken two years more to do this work. As TWZ has highlighted in years of reporting now, repairs to Connecticut , in general, were always set to be challenging and costly due to the small size of the Seawolf class and the design being long out of production. The Navy originally planned to acquire 29 of these boats, but ultimately bought just three as a result of post-Cold War drawdowns. In addition, shrinking the program of record so severely caused the unit price of each one to rise substantially, just over $10 billion in 2025 dollars. At the time of writing, they are still the most costly attack submarines ever built. The last of the Seawolf class submarines, the highly secretive USS Jimmy Carter , which entered service in 2005, is also a heavily modified sub-type optimized for underwater espionage missions . USS Connecticut at sea in 2009. USN It is also worth noting that the U.S. Navy, as well as some of its foreign counterparts , have repaired similarly severe damage to submarines by cannibalizing entire sections from decommissioned boats in the same class. However, this is not an option given the size of the Seawolf class and the still very high demand for them operationally . The core design offers advanced capabilities that make even USS Seawolf and USS Connecticut especially well suited to a variety of specialized tasks . This is clearly why the Navy has continued to invest so much in returning Connecticut to the fleet. As mentioned, repairs to Connecticut are now not expected to be finished until sometime in the summer of next year. This is the latest in a succession of schedule slips in recent years. The original goal had been for the boat to be back in service by September 2025. “The Navy’s target completion date for the availability is the summer of 2027. PSNS & IMF is dedicated to executing this work with the highest standards of safety, technical accuracy, and craftsmanship to ensure the ship returns to the fleet ready to take its place at the tip of the spear in defense of our nation’s interests,” a Navy official told TWZ in September. “Current work consists of structural and systems restoration and required lifecycle maintenance.” Earlier in the year, the Navy also revealed that it is now planning on sending Connecticut into retirement in 2031. This means the submarine has just four more years of service ahead of it if the current repair schedule holds. The Navy does have plans to acquire a new class of nuclear attack submarines, currently referred to as SSN(X). In the past, the service has described those future boats as more of a direct successor to the Seawolf class than the versions of the Virginia class it is buying now. A picture of the first-in-class USS Seawolf . USN “The analytical conclusion was unequivocal: to dominate high-end peer threats in the middle of this century, a clean sheet design is required. The Virginia class is a fantastic, unmatched world-class warship, and it will remain the backbone of our attack fleet for decades,” Navy Rear Adm. Andrew Miller said at the Naval Submarine League’s main annual conference last week, per USNI News . “As adversary capabilities evolve, we require expanded payload capacity, greater electrical and hydrodynamic margins and unprecedented architectural flexibility that simply cannot be backfitted into an existing hull form.” Miller is currently the head of the Undersea Warfare Division with the Office of the Chief of Naval Operations. In terms of desired key capabilities for SSN(X), the Navy wants “first, higher flank speed and tactical control speed. Two, improved operational availability. Three, decisive lethality. Four, superior stealth and layered survivability, and finally organic robotic and autonomous systems hosting and command and control,” Miller added. “We are redefining the role of the submarine from a standalone hunter-killer to a capital mothership. By launching uncrewed systems directly from submarine torpedo tubes and integrating unmanned [robotic] vehicles into our battle plans, we dramatically expand the tactical reach of our manned fleet.” The first SSN(X) submarines are not expected to begin entering service until the mid-2040s, at the earliest. The Navy will continue acquiring Virginia class submarines in the interim. This includes stretched Block IV and V versions with Virginia Payload Modules (VPM) that will now be categorized as guided-missile types (SSGN). There will also be a one-of-a-kind seabed warfare version of the Virginia , which could well take over for the USS Jimmy Carter. A briefing slide from General Dynamics Electric Boat detailing existing and future planned subvariants of the Virginia class nuclear submarine. The Block VI and V types have now been reclassified as nuclear-powered guided missile submarines (SSGN) rather than nuclear-powered attack submarines (SSN). General Dynamics Electric Boat When it comes to USS Connecticut , if there are no further delays, the fully repaired submarine with its new bow sonar dome should be back in service by the middle of next year. Chinese v American Views on WAR with Taiwan
Posted Aug 14, 2026 by Martin Armstrong |
The Center for Strategic and International Studies conducted an extraordinary survey of 64 leading experts on China, Taiwan, and cross-Strait relations, including 28 former senior U.S. government officials, 23 former government policy and intelligence analysts, and 13 academics and think-tank experts. What their answers reveal is not that China is preparing to invade Taiwan tomorrow, as the neocons would like everyone to believe, but that Beijing remains willing to wait so long as nobody crosses the line of formal Taiwanese independence. Some 84% said Beijing is willing to wait for unification but will not accept the status quo permanently, while only 10% believed China seeks unification at the earliest opportunity. Not one of the 64 experts believed Beijing would ever accept an independent Taiwan.
This is precisely why Taiwan has become so dangerous. The West keeps portraying the conflict as if Xi Jinping wakes up every morning staring at a calendar trying to decide when to launch an amphibious invasion. Yet 83% of these experts said China did not plan to use significant kinetic force against Taiwan by 2027, and 80% said China’s enormous 2022 military exercises did not indicate Beijing had accelerated its timetable. Only 6% of respondents outside the former senior government group saw 2027 as a hard deadline, while not one former senior U.S. official did. The obsession with 2027 has nevertheless become extremely useful for the military establishment because every supposed deadline becomes another justification for weapons, deployments, bases, and spending.
The survey found that 44% believed Beijing has a hard deadline of 2049, the centennial of the People’s Republic, while 42% believed China could wait indefinitely provided unification remains possible. This is an important distinction because China thinks in terms of generations while Western politicians think in terms of the next election. Beijing does not need to invade Taiwan if economic, political, and military pressure can gradually change the situation in its favor. Only 20% of those surveyed believed China even possessed a coherent roadmap for peaceful unification, which tells us this is not some perfectly scripted invasion plan sitting in Xi’s desk drawer.
Where the numbers become alarming is not an unprovoked invasion but what happens when politicians begin crossing China’s red lines. More than three-quarters of the experts, 77%, believed China would invade within six months if Taiwan formally declared independence. Among former senior U.S. officials, that number was 79%. Even some of those who did not expect an immediate invasion believed Beijing would respond with a blockade or enormous military exercises. This is why politicians encouraging Taiwan toward formal independence are playing with the lives of 23 million people. They can deliver all the speeches they want about democracy from Washington, London, or Brussels, but they will not be the civilians sitting underneath the missiles if their political experiment goes wrong.
Not one expert believed an explicit American commitment to defend Taiwan would cause China to invade immediately, but 64% believed Beijing would respond strongly enough to provoke a U.S.-China or China-Taiwan crisis, while another 31% expected a more limited negative response. Only two of the 64 experts believed formally committing America to Taiwan’s defense would actually deter China from using force because Beijing already assumes that the United States will intervene anyway.
A direct invasion is not even the most likely path toward conflict. Only 8% of the experts described an amphibious invasion within ten years as likely, while 63% called it possible and 27% unlikely. Force short of invasion received much higher probabilities, with 52% saying deliberate escalation such as a blockade was likely or very likely. An accidental military incident was considered even more dangerous, with 34% saying a collision or accident around the Taiwan Strait was likely and another 22% calling it very likely. When warships and aircraft from opposing nuclear powers continually operate around the same small body of water, war does not require some grand master plan. It requires one mistake followed by politicians who refuse to back down.
A later CSIS survey of American and Taiwanese experts reinforces that point. Roughly 90% of U.S. experts and 62% of Taiwanese experts believed China already possessed the capability to impose a law-enforcement-led quarantine that substantially reduces trade into Taiwan. Around 80% of American experts and 60% of Taiwanese experts believed Beijing could execute a PLA blockade, while Taiwanese experts were considerably more skeptical that China could successfully carry out an invasion. If Beijing wanted to coerce Taiwan during the following five years, experts considered a quarantine the most likely option. If China decided it wanted immediate unification, however, approximately 80% regarded a highly kinetic joint blockade as likely or very likely.
This is where the economic consequences become enormous because Taiwan does not need to be invaded for the world economy to be thrown into chaos. A quarantine or blockade would immediately threaten shipping, insurance, semiconductor supply chains, electronics, automobiles, communications equipment, and virtually every modern industry dependent upon advanced chips. The later CSIS survey found most American and Taiwanese experts did not believe Taiwan could withstand a Chinese blockade for longer than three months without substantial U.S. intervention. Washington would then face the decision nobody wants to discuss honestly: accept China’s blockade or attempt to break it militarily and risk direct war between two nuclear powers.
Taiwan is also the world’s semiconductor pressure point. The island’s importance to advanced chip manufacturing means a serious blockade would not remain a regional event. Factories thousands of miles away could discover that a conflict they thought had nothing to do with them suddenly prevents them from obtaining critical components. Markets would begin repricing the risk immediately, shipping premiums would explode, companies would scramble for inventory, and governments would discover once again how fragile global supply chains have become. This is why capital will react long before politicians formally declare that a war has begun.
What I find particularly revealing in the later CSIS survey is the difference between American confidence and Taiwanese confidence in Washington. An astonishing 96% of American experts were completely or moderately confident that the United States would intervene militarily if China invaded Taiwan during the following five years. Taiwanese experts were less confident in American intervention and considerably less confident that U.S. allies would join the fight. It is always easier for people thousands of miles away to be certain about somebody else’s war.
This is precisely why Taiwan remains one of the critical geopolitical pressure points as we move toward 2029. The danger is not simply that China arbitrarily decides to invade. The greater danger is escalation, miscalculation, political promises that cannot be withdrawn, and Western policymakers convincing themselves that every additional provocation somehow produces deterrence. China has made its position on formal independence perfectly clear, and even the experts inside the Western foreign-policy establishment overwhelmingly acknowledge that Beijing would react with force if that line were crossed.
If Taiwan declares formal independence, 77% of the experts surveyed believed China would invade within six months. That is not a statistic policymakers should treat as another war-game scenario. It is a warning about what happens when politicians deliberately remove the ambiguity that has helped keep the peace.

罗马——芬兰运营商 Iceye 向意大利火箭制造商 Avio 提出了 20 亿欧元现金报价（合 22 亿美元），该报价将整合欧洲的太空能力，并让 Iceye 负责 Avio 向美国导弹业务的扩张。拟议的交易符合减少对外部供应商的依赖并缩小与美国和中国行业领导者之间日益扩大的差距的努力。 “欧洲对主权太空和国防能力的需求正在增长。满足这一需求的工业能力建设需要数年时间，这使得现在投资至关重要，”Iceye 周二表示。该公司表示，将在五年内向意大利 Avio 投资 10 亿欧元，以扩大 Avio Vega 火箭的客户群。芬兰政府支持这一提议，芬兰国防部长安蒂·哈卡宁表示，“如果完成……将创建一个全球航天工业参与者，通过它，芬兰和整个欧洲国防的自给自足的供应安全将上升到一个新的水平。” Avio 周二表示正在考虑这一收购要约，而拥有 Avio 18% 股份的意大利国家控股国防集团 Leonardo 的首席执行官表示，他对这一收购要约感到“惊喜”，并将予以考虑。 Avio 董事会于周二举行了第一次会议，并表示已开始评估此次出价，Iceye 表示，该出价较该意大利集团周一收盘价溢价 21.3%，较其三个月成交量加权平均价溢价 34.8%。
除了欧洲航天发射活动外，Avio 也是导弹固体火箭发动机的市场领导者。9 月，该公司在弗吉尼亚州赫特的美国新设施破土动工，以实现为美国导弹生产带来急需的额外产能的雄心。 Avio 已与雷神公司合作生产 Mk 104 双推力火箭发动机，并与洛克希德·马丁公司合作在 Hurt 为洛克希德的增程 GMLRS (ER GMLRS) 和精确打击导弹 (PrSM) 项目生产发动机。 Avio 发言人告诉《防务新闻》，如果 Iceye 收购，则需要美国政府的批准以及意大利政府的批准。 9月，Avio宣布9个月的订单额为2.37亿欧元，其中一半与国防相关，其余主要与其Vega C和Vega E发射器有关。 Iceye 表示，其每股 41 欧元的报价将通过全资意大利子公司 Iris 2 发起，目的是使该公司退市。消息传出后，Avio 股价上涨超过 15%，至 39.5 欧元左右。 Iceye 自 2022 年以来一直向乌克兰提供卫星雷达图像，上个月与诺基亚和乌克兰国防部签署了一份意向书，探讨太空合作，包括主权卫星通信。
Iceye首席执行官拉法尔·莫德热夫斯基(Rafal Modrzewski)在赫尔辛基的一次活动上发表讲话时表示，该公司在发起竞标之前已与包括政府在内的相关各方进行了磋商，并且还需要几个月的时间才能完成交易。“这是一次非凡的能力组合……遵循相当明确的行业趋势，带来了全面的垂直整合，”莫德热夫斯基表示，并补充说这对两家公司都有利。材料来自路透社，作者 Giulia Segreti 和 Essi Lehto。

【原文 English Original】
ROME — Finnish operator Iceye has a made €2 billion cash offer ($2.2 billion) for Italian rocket maker Avio which would integrate Europe’s space capabilities as well as putting Iceye in charge of Avio’s expansion into the U.S. missile business. The proposed deal fits with efforts to reduce reliance on external providers and narrow a widening gap with industry leaders in the U.S. and China. “Europe’s need for sovereign space and defense capabilities is growing. Building the industrial capacity to meet that demand takes years, which makes it critical to invest now,” said Iceye on Tuesday. The firm said it would invest €1 billion in Avio in Italy over five years in a bid to expand the customer base of Avio’s Vega rocket. The Finnish government backed the offer, with Finnish Defense Minister Antti Hakkanen stating, “If completed … a global space industry player will be created, through which the self-sufficient security of supply of Finland’s and all of Europe’s defense will rise to a new level.” Avio said on Tuesday it was considering the offer, while the CEO of Italian state controlled defense group Leonardo, which owns an 18% percent stake in Avio, said he was “pleasantly surprised” by the bid and would consider it. Avio’s board held a first meeting on Tuesday and said it had started assessing the bid, which Iceye said offered a 21.3% premium to the Italian group’s closing price on Monday or a 34.8% premium to its three-month volume-weighted average price. Apart from its European space launch activity, Avio is also a market leader in solid rocket motors for missiles. In September it broke ground in Hurt, Virginia, on a new U..S facility to fulfill an ambition to bring much needed extra capacity to U.S. missile production. Avio has already partnered with Raytheon on production of the Mk 104 dual-thrust rocket motor and has teamed with Lockheed Martin to produce motors at Hurt for Lockheed’s Extended Range GMLRS (ER GMLRS) and Precision Strike Missile (PrSM) programs. An Avio spokesman told Defense News that U.S. government approval would be required in the event of a takeover by Iceye, as well as Italian government approval. In September, Avio announced a nine month order intake of €237 million, of which half was defense related, with the remainder mainly related to its Vega C and Vega E launchers. Iceye said its €41-per-share offer will be launched through wholly owned Italian subsidiary Iris 2 with the aim of delisting the company. Avio shares climbed more than 15% to around €39.5 on the news. Iceye has supplied Ukraine with satellite radar imagery since 2022, and last month signed a letter of intent with Nokia and Ukraine’s Defence Ministry to explore cooperation in space, including sovereign satellite communications. Speaking at an event in Helsinki, Iceye CEO Rafal Modrzewski said the company had held consultations with the parties involved, including governments, before launching the bid, and that it would take a few more months to close the transaction. “It’s a phenomenal combination of capabilities … bringing a full vertical integration, following quite clear industry trends,” Modrzewski said, adding that it would be beneficial for both companies. With material from Reuters by Giulia Segreti and Essi Lehto.

维也纳——美国、俄罗斯和中国领导人将于周四在中国科技大都市深圳会面，这场会议被各方誉为“历史性”会议。讨论的主题包括削减全球核库存。但专家警告说，虽然会议本身是一个积极的进展，但任何重大突破仍然不太可能。过去一周，人们对这次聚会的期望不断升高，尤其是在俄罗斯，这次活动被赋予了“雅尔塔2.0”的色彩，指的是1945年二战后重新安排世界秩序的会议。与此同时，从美国方面来看，特朗普政府在深圳推动有关削减核武器的讨论，令许多观察家感到惊讶。俄罗斯和美国之间的最后一项战略军备控制条约（《新削减战略武器条约》）于 2 月到期，这使得这两个最大的核国家自 1972 年以来首次对原子武库没有数量限制。与此同时，中国不是《新削减战略武器条约》的缔约国，事实上也从未加入过任何类似的战略武器条约。据估计，北京拥有世界第三大核武库，有数百个，尽管分析人士认为，中国近年来一直在努力大幅增加这一数字。美国和俄罗斯各自拥有约 4,000 件核武器库存。
这种数字上的差异也是中国此前对以三边形式讨论战略武器限制的想法感到愤怒的原因，就像美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在会议前夕推动的那样。尽管北京方面已经确认了此次会议，但并未正式表示战略武器对话将提上议程。中国外交部发言人毛宁表示，“三位元首将就维护世界和平、促进大国关系战略稳定深入交换意见。”这避免了明确指出美国的要求。 “总统已明确表示，除其他议题外，他将讨论世界范围内核武器的削减。特朗普总统认为，这种扩散非常危险，”白宫发言人奥利维亚·威尔士上周五告诉记者。总部位于维也纳的开放核网络（一家处理核军备控制问题的国际非政府组织）的研究协调员尼基塔·杰格蒂亚列夫（Nikita Degtyarev）表示，他对可实现的成果持现实态度。 “我没有很高的期望，但我很高兴这一切正在发生，”他在接受采访时说。 “领导人级别的会议不同于正在进行的五常对话和其他现有形式。”五常对话汇集了五个核不扩散条约承认的核武器国家——美国、俄罗斯、中国、法国和英国。

【原文 English Original】
VIENNA — The leaders of the U.S., Russia and China are set to meet in the Chinese tech metropolis of Shenzhen on Thursday in an event that has been hailed as “historic” by all sides. Among the topics raised for discussion are reductions in global nuclear stockpiles. But experts caution that while the meeting itself is a positive development, any major breakthrough remains unlikely.  Expectations for the get-together ratcheted up over the course of the past week, particularly in Russia, where the event has been ascribed undertones of a “Yalta 2.0,” referencing the 1945 conference that reordered the world after World War II. From the U.S. side, meanwhile, the Trump administration surprised many observers by pushing for discussions about reducing nuclear weapons while in Shenzhen. The last strategic arms control treaty between Russia and the U.S., in the form of New START, expired in February, leaving the two largest nuclear states without numerical limits on atomic arsenals  for the first time since 1972.  China, meanwhile, was not a party to New START and was, in fact, never part of any strategic arms treaty like it. Beijing is estimated to have the third-largest nuclear arsenal in the world, at several hundred, although analysts believe it has been working to significantly increase this number in recent years. The U.S. and Russia each have stockpiles of around 4,000  nuclear weapons.  This numerical discrepancy is also why China has previously bristled at the idea of discussing strategic arms limitation in a trilateral format like the one U.S. President Donald Trump has been pushing in the run-up to the meeting. Although Beijing has confirmed the meeting, it has stopped short of officially saying strategic arms dialogue would be on the agenda. “The three presidents will have an in-depth exchange of views on safeguarding world peace and enabling strategic stability in major-country relations,” said Mao Ning, spokesperson for the Chinese Foreign Ministry.  This avoids naming explicitly what the U.S. has asked for. “The President has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world. This proliferation, President Trump believes, is very dangerous,” White House spokesperson Olivia Wales told reporters last Friday.  Nikita Degtyarev, research coordinator at the Vienna-based Open Nuclear Network, an international NGO dealing with nuclear arms control, said he was realistic about achievable outcomes. “I don’t have very high expectations, but I’m happy that it’s happening,” he said in an interview. “A meeting at the leader level is something else than the ongoing P5 dialogue and other existing formats.” The P5 dialogue brings together the five Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty-recognized nuclear weapons states – the U.S., Russia, China, France and the U.K. – on a working level to discuss nuclear policy and risk reduction.  “If there is any outcome of the trilateral meeting relating to nuclear issues, it will likely be more of a political statement than a verifiable and restrictive arms control agreement,” said Heather Williams, director of the Project on Nuclear Issues and senior fellow at the Washington-based think tank CSIS ,  “I think the most likely significant outcome would be a reiteration of the Reagan-Gorbachev mantra that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought,” Degtyarev said. A more substantive or groundbreaking agreement was also unlikely because there simply wasn’t enough time for lower-level officials to hammer out the details of any possible agreement that the leaders could sign, he said. Major arms control treaties often take years of meticulous crafting at the working level before heads of state come together to sign them.  Trump first raised the topic of denuclearization in the context of the summit to reporters on Oct. 19, a day after the Wall Street Journal first reported about a proposed trilateral meeting.  A possible wildcard agenda item remains in the form of artificial intelligence in nuclear weapons. AI in nuclear command and control has emerged as a somewhat more promising topic and a potential area for agreement more palatable to all sides than commitments to numerical reductions or verification mechanisms. The South China Morning Post reported Nov. 11, citing sources familiar with preparations, that working-level teams had discussed AI in critical weapons systems and that the agenda was shifting toward potential common ground, particularly AI’s role in nuclear command and control. One source characterized AI governance of nuclear weapons as an “easy deliverable” consistent with past policies. This “could give Trump something to announce without requiring anyone to compromise their nuclear posture,” Lizzi Lee, a fellow at the Asia Society Policy Institute, told the French press agency AFP .  Under the previous U.S. administration, Biden and Xi reaffirmed the importance of human decision-making in nuclear command and control in November 2024, while Russia has so far resisted such language, including in the P5 process.  Much may depend on the willingness of Beijing to engage in strategic arms dialogue, which has indicated it has no major desire to discuss this topic while China remains a numerical underdog in the quantity of its warheads. “China is the host and will probably closely stage-manage the event and the agenda,” Degtyarev said. Xi Jinping’s style of international engagements tends to be highly scripted and predictable, at odds with Trump’s more improvisational approach.  The common denominator for all three leaders is more likely to be good publicity. “Trump is probably genuine about his interest in nuclear arms reduction,” Degtyarev assessed, “but probably also from a self-serving and PR point of view.”  Though the meeting is historic in nature for its assembling of a triumvirate of the world’s most powerful men, “the Yalta 2.0 comparisons are overblown,” said Degtyarev. “The scale of the historical moment is simply different.”

zh_title: 美国政府确认对黄仁勋丑闻核心新加坡公司进行刑事调查
summary: 美国司法部和商务部已确认对 Megaspeed 进行刑事调查，并发表联合声明称，他们将“对 Megaspeed 可能发生的任何犯罪行为采取全面法律制裁”。当局认为，Megaspeed 是众多可能规避出口规则的公司之一，这些规则旨在限制向经批准的公司和国家销售先进的人工智能芯片，例如英伟达制造的芯片。该公司是最近黄仁勋丑闻的核心，他上周从该公司辞职。古迪
content:
美国司法部和商务部已确认对 Megaspeed 进行刑事调查，并发表联合声明称，他们将“对 Megaspeed 可能发生的任何犯罪行为采取全面法律制裁”。当局认为，Megaspeed 是众多可能规避出口规则的公司之一，这些规则旨在限制向经批准的公司和国家销售先进的人工智能芯片，例如英伟达制造的芯片。该公司是最近黄仁勋丑闻的核心，他上周从该公司辞职。深入了解 TH Premium：台湾、贸易和关税（图片来源：tsmc） 虽然美国在芯片制裁上反复无常，但中国正在建立自己的芯片供应市场 中国长达十年的半导体推动状况 华为 Ascend NPU 路线图审查了中国长鑫存储的目标，到 2030 年，第六座大型晶圆厂将占据 30% 的 DRAM 内存市场份额 中国最新一轮稀土出口管制解释说，Megaspeed 已被添加到 Nvidia 的禁售名单中声明显示，该清单将于 2025 年 6 月列入清单，但《纽约时报》的一篇报道称，马来西亚 Megaspeed 子公司在该日期后整整八个月内继续收到大量 Nvidia 芯片。据信，英伟达受出口管制的 Blackwell 和 H200 芯片是通过第三方或直接从英伟达本身运往 Speedmatrix，然后再转交给中国。
Nvidia 辩称，它已获得美国商务部的许可，可以向 Megaspeed 运送组件。值得注意的是，Nvidia 继续将 Megaspeed 列为云合作伙伴。商务部于 2024 年首次启动对 Megaspeed 的调查，原因是其可能存在出口违规行为，随后展开了新的刑事调查。到 2025 年 5 月，它已要求英伟达提供与其向 Megaspeed 销售相关的数据，到 6 月，官员们访问了 Megaspeed，甚至采访了据称是中国间谍的现任前高管 Alice Huang。黄女士也是时任英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋在本月初辞职前曾有过外遇的女性。在那次访问之后，司法部牵头对 Megaspeed 进行了调查。商务部和司法部关于 Megaspeed 调查的联合声明。 https://t.co/aAdtN9aDfF 2026 年 11 月 17 日 Megaspeed 长期以来一直被指控为人工智​​能组件走私活动的幌子。 2025 年 10 月，一项调查声称，该公司通过进口然后再出口到中国，帮助将价值约 20 亿美元的 Nvidia 芯片转移到中国。 Megaspeed 表示，公司遵守所有法律，而且风流丑闻的核心女性黄女士已不再在公司工作。中国政府也驳回了有关她是国家间谍的说法。
商务部和司法部的联合声明指出，迄今为止，该公司在起诉芯片走私者方面有着良好的记录。迄今为止，在总共六项调查中，已有 17 名被告受到指控，而且可能还会有更多被告受到指控。一名加州男子最近因被指控向中国走私价值超过 3 亿美元的受出口限制的 Nvidia 芯片而被捕。他现在面临最高20年的监禁。

【原文 English Original】
A criminal investigation into Megaspeed has been confirmed by the United States Justice and Commerce Departments, with a joint statement saying that they will “bring the full extent of the law against Megaspeed for any criminal conduct that may have occurred.” Authorities believe that Megaspeed is one of a raft of companies that may have circumvented export rules designed to limit the sale of advanced AI chips, like those built by Nvidia, to approved companies and countries. The company is at the heart of the recent Jensen Huang scandal, which saw him resign from the company last week . Go deeper with TH Premium: Taiwan, trade, and tariffs (Image credit: tsmc) While the U.S. flip-flops on chip sanctions, China is building its own chip supply market The state of China's decade-long semiconductor push Huawei Ascend NPU roadmap examined China's CXMT targets 30% DRAM memory market share by 2030 with sixth mega-fab China's latest round of rare-earth export controls explained Megaspeed was added to Nvidia's no-sell list in June 2025, the statement reveals, but a New York Times report claims that a Malaysian Megaspeed subsidiary continued to receive large shipments of Nvidia chips for a full eight months after that date. It's believed that Nvidia's export-controlled Blackwell and H200 chips were shipped to Speedmatrix, either via third parties or directly from Nvidia itself, before being handed off to China. Nvidia has argued that it was given Commerce Department permission to ship the components to Megaspeed. Notably, Nvidia continues to list Megaspeed as a cloud partner. The new criminal investigation follows a Commerce Department investigation into Megaspeed that first kicked off in 2024 over possible export violations. By May 2025, it had requested Nvidia's data relating to sales it made to Megaspeed, and by June, officials visited Megaspeed and even interviewed Alice Huang, the now-former executive who is allegedly a Chinese spy . Ms. Huang is also the woman that then-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with before resigning his position earlier this month . Following that visit, the Justice Department took the lead in the investigation into Megaspeed. Joint Statement from Department of Commerce and Department of Justice on Megaspeed Investigation. https://t.co/aAdtN9aDfF November 17, 2026 Megaspeed has long been accused of being a front for an AI component smuggling operation. In October 2025, an investigation claimed that it had helped move around $2 billion worth of Nvidia chips into China by importing them and then re-exporting them to the country. Megaspeed says that it complies with all laws and that the woman at the center of the affair scandal, Ms. Huang, is no longer at the company. The Chinese government has also dismissed claims that she was a state spy. The joint Commerce and Justice Departments' statement pointed to its strong track record when prosecuting chip smugglers to date. 17 defendants across a total of six investigations have been charged so far, with more likely to follow. A Californian man was recently arrested after being accused of smuggling more than $300 million worth of export-restricted Nvidia chips to China. He now faces up to 20 years in prison.

这一言论遭到了美国大使贾里德·诺维利的严厉谴责，他表示美国和新西兰是建立在民主基础上的，并称布朗的言论具有冒犯性。
惠灵顿 — — 新西兰最大城市的市长表示，民主已经“走到尽头”，是时候尝试另一种形式的政府了，同时赞扬了中国的一党制。
奥克兰市长韦恩·布朗告诉媒体Stuff，他在访问中国大城市广州期间观看了新西兰最近的选举。
“我不知道新西兰发生了什么，”他在 11 月 17 日发表的采访中说道。
“这是一个深不可测的制度……看看美国的选举……产生了一个不工作的政府。欧洲多年来没有经历过一次好的选举。”
“民主已经走到了尽头。真的是时候做点别的事情了，”他补充道。
新西兰于 11 月进行了民意调查，但结果仍然难以预测，预计联合政府谈判将在 11 月 27 日最终结果公布时开始。
当被问及他提出的民主替代方案是什么时，布朗说他不想卷入意识形态。
“什么在起作用？中国在起作用。你知道，在经济增长和繁荣方面，”他说。
近年来，随着世界第二大经济体努力支撑内需并扭转支出下滑，中国经济增长放缓。
北京还被指控广泛侵犯人权，包括针对少数民族的人权，言论自由受到限制，任何反对执政的共产党的行为都被压制。
布朗的言论引发了华盛顿驻惠灵顿大使贾里德·诺维利的罕见谴责。
“我认为新西兰政府需要最低限度的情报才能接收情报简报；从市长的声明中可以明显看出，他没有达到这一要求，”诺夫利在 X 上说道。
“美国和新西兰并没有因为认为赋予人民发言权太麻烦而建立了两个成功的民主国家。”
随后他告诉新西兰国家广播公司，布朗似乎已被中国“俘获”。
他表示，他很高兴有机会与市长交谈，“但你知道，要通过他门上的危险信号可能会很困难”。
新西兰与美国、英国、加拿大和澳大利亚一样是“五眼”情报共享联盟的成员。
这个岛国因对中国采取更温和的立场而受到批评——将其贸易关系置于盟友的安全担忧之上。
然而，近年来，威灵顿的立场有时公开对北京采取强硬态度，情报机构八月份的一份报告指责中国从事间谍活动，但其大使馆强烈否认了这一点。
布朗自 2022 年起担任奥克兰市长，以煽动性言论而闻名，其中包括提及一名印度裔记者

New Zealand mayor says democracy has ‘had its day’ after China visit

Auckland’s Mayor Wayne Brown said it was time to try another form of government while lauding China’s one-party system.
Published Nov 18, 2026, 02:11 PM
Updated Nov 18, 2026, 03:28 PM
Auckland Mayor Wayne Brown said democracy has “had its day” after visiting Guangzhou, and praised China’s one-party system for “economic growth and prosperity”.
His remarks came as New Zealand’s election remained too close to call, with coalition talks due after final results on Nov 27.
The comments drew a sharp rebuke from US ambassador Jared Novelly, who said the US and New Zealand were built on democracy and called Brown’s remarks offensive.
WELLINGTON – The mayor of New Zealand’s largest city said democracy has “had its day” and it was time to try another form of government while lauding China’s one-party system.
Auckland’s Mayor Wayne Brown told media outlet Stuff he had watched New Zealand’s recent election during a trip to the Chinese mega-city of Guangzhou.
“I don’t know what’s going on in New Zealand,” he said in the interview published on Nov 17.
“It’s an unfathomable system... and look at the election in America... produced a sort of non-working government. Europe hasn’t had a good election for years.”
“Democracy’s had its day. It’s time for something else, really,” he added.
New Zealand went to the polls in November but the result remains too close to call, with coalition negotiations expected to begin when final results are released on Nov 27.
Asked what his proposed alternative to democracy would be, Brown said that he did not want to get involved in ideology.
“What’s working? China’s working. You know, in terms of economic growth and prosperity,” he said.
China’s growth has slowed in recent years as the world’s second-largest economy struggles to prop up domestic demand and reverse a spending slump.
Beijing is also accused of widespread rights violations, including against ethnic minorities, with freedom of expression curtailed and any opposition to its ruling Communist Party stamped out.
Brown’s comments sparked a rare rebuke from Washington’s ambassador in Wellington Jared Novelly.
“I suppose New Zealand government requires a minimum level of intelligence to receive an intelligence briefing; it’s obvious from his statements the mayor hasn’t made the cut,” Novelly said on X.
“The United States and New Zealand didn’t build two successful democracies by deciding that giving people a say was too much trouble.”
He then told state broadcaster RNZ that it seemed Brown had been “captured” by China.
He said he welcomed the opportunity to talk with the mayor, “but you know, it might be tough to get through the red flag on his door”.
New Zealand is a member of the “Five Eyes” intelligence-sharing alliance alongside the United States, Britain, Canada, and Australia.
The island nation has been criticised for taking a softer line on China – putting its trading relationship ahead of its allies’ security concerns.
However, Wellington’s stance has at times publicly hardened against Beijing in recent years with an August intelligence agency report accusing China of espionage, which its embassy strongly denied.
Brown has been mayor of Auckland since 2022 and is known for incendiary outbursts, including referring to a journalist of Indian descent as a “Muslim terrorist”. AFP

普京预计特朗普和习近平亚太经合组织会议将受益海峡时报
普京在抨击制裁时强调俄罗斯对亚太经合组织的韧性

俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京表示，在全球经济碎片化和军事政治风险的背景下，需要建立伙伴关系。
发表于 2026 年 11 月 18 日 12:25
更新于 2026 年 11 月 18 日 04:41
普京对亚太经合组织表示，俄罗斯在制裁下蓬勃发展，是亚太贸易的重要合作伙伴，但文章称俄罗斯经济已经放缓，并面临战争和制裁压力。
他赞扬与习近平的更密切关系，并表示会谈可能涵盖乌克兰以及计划与特朗普的会面，这表明俄罗斯对中国的依赖日益加深。
普京攻击欧盟，并声称俄罗斯有“尊严”和“全速前进”，但文章称，这与经济增长疲弱、炼油厂关闭和天然气谈判陷入僵局相冲突。
中国深圳——弗拉基米尔·普京总统表示，尽管受到国际制裁，俄罗斯仍在蓬勃发展，将其吹捧为模范伙伴，并将他所描绘的俄罗斯的积极前景与日渐衰弱的欧洲的前景进行了对比。
普京在中国向亚太经合组织（APEC）商界领袖发表讲话时驳斥了“孤立我国的失败尝试”，并坚称俄罗斯正在“有尊严地”克服挑战。
11 月 18 日，在与习近平主席会面之前，普京在深圳举行的亚太经合组织工商领导人峰会上表示：“我们已准备好分享我们的经验。” “我们正在全速前进，甚至比我们预想的还要快，我们愿继续推进同亚太地区的互利合作。”
普京正寻求利用他在世界舞台上难得的机会来宣传俄罗斯不仅是一个理想的经商之地，而且还是一个充满活力的经济体，具有巨大的未开发潜力，是亚太经合组织成员国的重要合作伙伴。
事实上，俄罗斯经济已经大幅放缓。
不管怎样，他的乐观态度表明这位克里姆林宫领导人在看到自己康复的迹象时是多么大胆，尽管他因对乌克兰发动近五年的战争而受到国际逮捕令和多轮制裁。
普京将于 11 月 18 日与世界上最重要的两位政府领导人习近平和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普一起参加三边峰会。
在 11 月 18 日与习近平会晤开始时的公开讲话中，他赞扬了两国在“困难的地缘政治环境”下在外国领域的伙伴关系，称双方都追求“旨在塑造更加公平的多极世界秩序的建设性方法”。
据克里姆林宫称，俄罗斯领导人将与习近平就包括乌克兰冲突在内的重大国际和地区问题进行广泛会谈。
据国际文传电讯社援引普京外交政策助手尤里·乌沙科夫的话报道，预计他将向习近平通报他与美方的最新接触情况，两国领导人可能会讨论计划中的与特朗普的三边会谈。
即将出席深圳亚太经合组织峰会的特朗普表示，他也对与普京进行一对一会谈持开放态度。
这是俄罗斯总统与习近平自 2026 年初以来的第五次会面，凸显了莫斯科与北京之间关系的紧密程度。
它还说明，自普京于 2022 年初对乌克兰发动全面战争以来，俄罗斯如何变得越来越依赖中国，因为制裁和与欧洲的大部分贸易崩溃迫使莫斯科重新调整通讯方向。

Putin expects benefit from Trump, Xi APEC meeting | The Straits Times
Putin pitches Russian resilience to APEC in swipe at sanctions
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
Russian President Vladimir Putin said partnership is needed amid a fragmented global economy and military-political risks.
Published Nov 18, 2026, 12:25 PM
Updated Nov 18, 2026, 04:41 PM
Putin told APEC Russia is thriving under sanctions and is a key partner for Asia-Pacific trade, but the article says Russia’s economy has slowed and faces war and sanction pressure.
He praised closer ties with Xi Jinping and said talks may cover Ukraine and a planned meeting with Trump, showing Russia’s growing reliance on China.
Putin attacked the EU and claimed Russia has “dignity” and “full speed ahead”, but the article says this clashes with weak growth, refinery shutdowns and stalled gas talks.
SHENZHEN, China – President Vladimir Putin said Russia was thriving despite international sanctions, touting it as a model partner and contrasting what he portrayed as his country’s positive outlook with those of a weakening Europe.
In a speech to Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) business leaders in China, Putin dismissed “failed attempts to isolate our country” and asserted that Russia was overcoming the challenges “with dignity”.
“We are ready to share our experience,” Putin told the APEC CEO Summit in Shenzhen on Nov 18, before meeting with President Xi Jinping. “We are moving at full speed ahead, even faster than we had predicted, and we are ready to continue moving forward in the development of mutually beneficial cooperation with the Asia-Pacific region.”
Putin is seeking to use his rare moment on the world stage to sell Russia as not just a desirable place to do business, but also a dynamic economy with huge untapped potential that represents an essential partner for APEC members.
In reality, Russia’s economy has slowed sharply.
His bullish outreach, regardless, shows how the Kremlin leader is emboldened at signs of his rehabilitation, despite being subject to an international arrest warrant and multiple rounds of sanctions as a result of the war on Ukraine he’s been waging for almost five years.
Putin is due to take part in a trilateral summit on Nov 18 with Xi and US President Donald Trump – the world’s two most important government leaders.
In public remarks at the start of his meeting with Xi on Nov 18, he praised their partnership in the foreign domain amid “a difficult geopolitical environment”, saying that both pursued “constructive approaches aimed at shaping a fairer multipolar world order”.
The Russian leader was due to hold extensive talks with Xi on major international and regional issues including the conflict in Ukraine, according to the Kremlin.
He is expected to brief Xi on his latest contacts with the US side, and the leaders are likely to discuss the planned trilateral talks with Trump, Interfax news wire reported, citing Putin’s foreign policy aide, Yuri Ushakov.
Trump, who is due to attend the APEC summit in Shenzhen, said that he was also open to a one-on-one with Putin.
The Russian president’s meeting with Xi is their fifth since the start of 2026, underscoring the intensity of ties between Moscow and Beijing.
It also speaks to how Russia has become increasingly dependent on China since Putin began his all-out war on Ukraine in early 2022, as sanctions and the collapse of much of its trade with Europe pushed Moscow to redirect commerce, finance and technology links eastwards.
In his speech, Putin singled out the European Union for criticism, saying that the 27-nation bloc was “losing its industrial capacity and its competitive position”, with rising debt loads hurting business and citizens witnessing a “humiliating” decline in living standards.
By contrast, the outside pressure “has provided Russia with a powerful incentive”, he said.
His speech drifted into fantasy in parts, asserting that Russia was Europe’s largest economy – it is not – and stressing its major logistics capabilities, a claim that stretches belief given that Ukraine is conducting strikes on Russian infrastructure including bridges, oil refineries and warehouses.
Russia’s economy has suffered as businesses and consumers wrestle with high interest rates imposed to slow inflation amid massive government spending on the war. Gross domestic product grew 1% in the third quarter, following a 1.3% expansion in the previous three months, as Ukrainian attacks knocked out industrial facilities, disrupted logistics and added to inflationary pressures.
Shutdowns at oil refineries drove an 18% year-on-year decline in refining output in the third quarter, the steepest drop in comparable quarterly figures going back to 2020, according to data from the Federal Statistics Service.
Putin brought a large delegation to China that includes dozens of top officials and executives from some of the country’s biggest companies and banks, including Rosneft, Novatek and Gazprom.
According to Russia’s Foreign Ministry, bilateral trade in the first 10 months of 2026 exceeded the total for all of 2025, rising by almost 33% to US$242.5 billion (S$312.77 billion).
Energy remains the main driver, but cooperation has expanded beyond traditional oil and gas supplies into large petrochemical projects, Russian-designed nuclear reactors in China and renewable-energy initiatives, according to Moscow.
One notable area where progress still appears elusive is over a contract that could more than double Russia’s current pipeline gas exports to China.
Russia’s gas giant Gazprom PJSC has for years been trying to reach a deal on supplies via the future Power of Baikal route, previously known as Power of Siberia 2. Details on pricing and volume flexibility have been among the stumbling blocks in talks, even as Russian officials have repeatedly said that remaining difficulties could be resolved quickly.
Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said in October that Gazprom and China National Petroleum Corp may reach a commercial agreement by the end of 2026.
Putin told the business forum that there was great potential benefit from the planned trilateral meeting with Xi and Trump.
“Moscow really wants this and is excited about the potential summit more than anybody else for a very clear reason – Moscow is the weakest power among the three,” said Alexander Gabuev, director of the Carnegie Russia Eurasia Centre.
If it goes ahead, for Putin, “it’s a matter of symbolic positioning of himself into this kind of league of superpower and the top boys that are sitting at the table”.
Russia, though, “is absolutely not in this league of top tier level powers anymore and is not coming back regardless of the outcome of Putin’s cruel war in Ukraine”, he said. BLOOMBERG

summary: 夏威夷珍珠港——导弹驱逐舰迈克尔·墨菲号在经过 346 天的部署（其中包括在南中国海的行动、12 次有争议地穿越霍尔木兹海峡、43 次海上补给以及 10 个月后撤换其指挥官）之后于周四返航，受到了草裙舞者和海峡上空延伸的彩虹的欢迎。尽管这艘航空母舰于 10 月 8 日返回圣地亚哥基地，但其大部分部署时间都隶属于亚伯拉罕·林肯号航母打击群。但它可能打破的任何部署长度记录都是短暂的。斯普鲁亚
content:
夏威夷珍珠港——导弹驱逐舰迈克尔·墨菲号在经过 346 天的部署（其中包括在南中国海的行动、12 次有争议地穿越霍尔木兹海峡、43 次海上补给以及 10 个月后撤换其指挥官）之后于周四返航，受到了草裙舞者和海峡上空延伸的彩虹的欢迎。尽管这艘航空母舰于 10 月 8 日返回圣地亚哥基地，但其大部分部署时间都隶属于亚伯拉罕·林肯号航母打击群。但它可能打破的任何部署长度记录都是短暂的。另一艘阿利伯克级驱逐舰斯普鲁恩斯号在经过 12 个月的部署后于今天返回家园，驻日本的约翰·芬恩号船员被告知预计将进行 13 至 14 个月的部署。正如《防务一号》10 月 22 日报道的那样，海军官员告诉家属，在可预见的未来，部署时间预计为 10 到 10 个月，这与近几十年来典型的 7 个月部署形成鲜明对比。海军最高军士长、海军军士长约翰·佩里曼 (John Perryman) 一周后证实了这一点，并表示至少在未来几年内，10 至 11 个月将成为常态。迈克尔·墨菲号中校表示，“迈克尔·墨菲”号于 2025 年 12 月 1 日离开夏威夷，穿过南中国海和马六甲海峡，然后到达北阿拉伯海，并在那里度过了大部分部署时间。大卫·尼古拉斯一个月前接任这艘驱逐舰的指挥。
尼古拉斯说，“迈克尔·墨菲”号在“史诗狂怒”行动期间发动了“战斧”导弹袭击，并参与了霍尔木兹海峡的封锁。“我非常自豪能够成为这个团队的一员，”他说。 “这是我有幸共事过的最有韧性的团队。”尼古拉斯此前指挥过另一艘导弹驱逐舰奥斯卡·奥斯汀号。据海军新闻稿称，当他于 9 月 10 日将掌权交给继任者时，他将成为罗德岛州水面作战学校的教官。但一名海军官员向《防务一号》证实，当“迈克尔·墨菲”号的前任上司中校改变了他的计划。凯特琳·坎宁安 (Caitlin Cunningham) 在执掌约 11 个月后，因“失去信心”而于 9 月 27 日被解职。在周四的返校节上，三等士官杰西·布莱森第一个下船，成为“初吻”抽奖的获胜者。他和妻子阿里安娜·里奥斯站在一起，开玩笑说这次部署涉及“大量的水”。 “加入海军，看看世界——但世界 70% 都是水，”他笑着说。但是，他补充说，工作人员很棒。 “我认为你可以把这艘船上的任何人放在任何其他船上，他们都会脱颖而出，”布莱森说。 ]]>

PEARL HARBOR, Hawaii —After a 346-day deployment that included operations in the South China Sea, 12 contested transits of the Strait of Hormuz, 43 replenishments at sea and the removal of its commander 10 months in, the guided-missile-destroyer Michael Murphy returned home Thursday, welcomed by hula dancers and a rainbow stretching over the channel. The ship was attached to the Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group for much of its deployment, though the aircraft carrier returned to its home in San Diego on Oct. 8. But any deployment-length records it may have broken were short lived. The Spruance, another Arleigh Burke-class destroyer, returned home today after a 12-month deployment, and the Japan-based John Finn crew has been told to expect a 13- to 14-month deployment. As Defense One reported on Oct. 22, Navy officials have told families to expect 10- to 10-month deployments for the foreseeable future—a stark contrast from the typical 7-month deployments of recent decades. The Navy’s top enlisted sailor, Master Chief Petty Officer of the Navy John Perryman, confirmed that a week later, saying 10-11 months will be the norm for at least a few years. The Micheal Murphy left Hawaii on Dec. 1, 2025, and sailed through the South China Sea and Strait of Malacca before reaching the North Arabian Sea, where it spent the bulk of the deployment, said Cmdr. David Nicolas, who took command of the destroyer a month ago. The Michael Murphy launched Tomahawk missile strikes during Operation Epic Fury and took part in the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, Nicolas said. “I’m incredibly proud to be part of this team,” he said. “This is the most resilient crew that I’ve had the pleasure to serve with.” Nicolas previously commanded the Oscar Austin, another guided-missile destroyer. When he handed over the helm to his successor on Sept. 10, he was slated to become an instructor at Surface Warfare Schools in Rhode Island, according to a Navy press release . But a Navy official confirmed to Defense One that his plans were changed when the Michael Murphy’s previous boss, Cmdr. Caitlin Cunningham, was relieved on Sept. 27 due to a “loss of confidence” after roughly 11 months in charge.    At Thursday’s homecoming, Petty Officer 3rd Class Jesse Bryson was first off the ship, as the winner of the “first kiss” raffle. Standing with his wife, Arianna Rios, he joked that the deployment involved “a lot of water.” “Join the Navy, see the world—but the world is 70-percent water,” he said with a laugh. But, he added, the crew was great. “I think you could put anyone from this ship on any other ship and they’d stand out,” Bryson said. ]]>

title: Taipei 101 lit up in support of Jensen Huang
zh_title: 台北101亮灯支持黄仁勋
summary: 英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋辞职后，台湾的一座摩天大楼成为了一系列支持这位被罢免的创始人的信息的背景，这位被罢黜的创始人承认与一名被指控为中国政府间谍的女性有染。此后，美国政府宣布对这名女子所在的公司 Megaspeed 进行刑事调查，原因是担心该公司可能帮助违反了与 Nvidia AI 芯片相关的出口管制。尽管如此，据中央通讯社报道，11 月 10 日晚上，台北 101 大楼的外部投射了信息
content:
英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋辞职后，台湾的一座摩天大楼成为了一系列支持这位被罢免的创始人的信息的背景，这位被罢黜的创始人承认与一名被指控为中国政府间谍的女性有染。此后，美国政府宣布对这名女子所在的公司 Megaspeed 进行刑事调查，原因是担心该公司可能帮助违反了与 Nvidia AI 芯片相关的出口管制。尽管如此，据中央通讯社报道，11 月 16 日晚，台北 101 大楼的外部投射了信息。这些信息包括“台湾 ♡ 詹森”、“家庭 ♡ 友谊”和“共同成长”，其驱动力可能是黄在该国近乎名人般的知名度。这种名人地位让台湾民众对黄的同情心不断增长，台湾科技行业的人士齐心协力为该项目提供资金。据报道，一名科技人员表示，这次灯光秀是为了“带回黄仁勋”，表达台湾的关切。台北 101 大楼亮灯支持丑闻缠身的黄仁勋 周一晚上，台北 101 大楼亮起支持黄仁勋的信息，几天前，黄仁勋因婚外情被曝光，国家安全问题受到越来越多的关注，辞去了英伟达首席执行官的职务。 https://t.co/VOtX1RX5qN 2026 年 11 月 16 日 这种担忧可能不需要太久了。
最近的报道表明，黄仁勋在递交辞呈几天后，可能正在密谋重返英伟达最高职位。SpaceX 首席执行官埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 和 Epic Games 首席执行官蒂姆·斯威尼 (Tim Sweeney) 已经大力支持黄仁勋重返英伟达的想法。迫使英伟达董事会下手的呼声也蔓延到了白宫，美国总统特朗普也呼吁让这位前首席执行官复职。尽管他的爱人是否是中国间谍，以及如果是的话，黄对这一事实可能了解多少，仍然存在不确定性。然而，特朗普表示，黄没有将国家安全置于危险之中。就其本身而言，据信英伟达董事会不会认真考虑允许黄继续他辞职前留下的工作。一位消息人士告诉 CNBC，该公司正专注于调查黄的行为和国家安全调查，而不是讨论他的回归。毫无疑问，这项调查还将考虑有关黄仁勋另一起婚外情的报道，这次是与英伟达高管。目前，英伟达前首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯(Colette Kress)担任临时首席执行官。克雷斯没过多久就迎来了第一个重大考验——丑闻发生以来该公司的首次财报电话会议将于今天（11 月 17 日）举行。

【原文 English Original】
Following the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang , a Taiwanese skyscraper became the backdrop for a series of messages in support of the ousted founder, who admitted to having an affair with a woman who has been accused of being a spy for the Chinese government . The U.S. government has since announced a criminal investigation into the company the woman worked for, Megaspeed, over concerns it may have aided in the breaking of export controls related to Nvidia AI chips. Despite that fact, CNA reports that the Taipei 101 building saw messages projected onto its exterior on the night of November 16. The messages included “Taiwan ♡ Jensen,” “Family ♡ Friendship,” and “Thrive Together,” with the driving force likely to be Huang's almost celebrity-like level of fame in the country. That celebrity status has seen public sympathy for Huang grow within Taiwan, with people within the country's technology industry coming together to fund the project. One technology worker reportedly said that the light show was supposed to “bring back Jensen Huang” and show Taiwan's concern. Taipei 101 lights up in support of scandal-hit Jensen HuangTaipei 101 lit up with messages of support for Jensen Huang on Monday evening, days after he resigned as Nvidia CEO amid revelations about his extramarital affairs & mounting scrutiny over national security concerns. https://t.co/VOtX1RX5qN November 16, 2026 That concern may not be needed for too much longer. Recent reports suggest that Huang could be plotting a return to the top job at Nvidia just days after he handed in his resignation. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney have already thrown their weight behind the idea of Huang's return to Nvidia. The clamor to force the hand of Nvidia's board has also extended to the White House, with U.S. President Trump also calling for the former CEO to be reinstated . This is despite ongoing uncertainty over whether his love interest was a Chinese spy and, if so, how much Huang may have known about that fact. Trump, however, says that Huang did not put national security at risk. For its part, it isn't believed that the Nvidia board is seriously considering allowing Huang to pick up where he left off pre-resignation. A source told CNBC that the company is focused on investigating Huang's conduct and a national security investigation and is not discussing his return. That investigation will no doubt also consider reports that Huang had another affair, this time with an Nvidia executive . For now, Nvidia's former CFO Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO. Kress hasn't had long to settle in ahead of the first big test — the company's first earnings call since the scandal will take place today, November 17.

title: 徵信社助中共跟監八炯 陸委會斥「背骨惡行」決不寬貸
summary: 【大紀元2026年11月18日訊】（大紀元記者戴德蔓台灣台北報導）台灣徵信業者涉嫌接受中共公安機關指示，非法蒐集網紅「八炯」、「閩南狼」及家屬個資，並派員跟監、拍攝，將情資交付中共公安機關。陸委會11月17日嚴厲譴責，這已非單純個資侵害，而是中共透過在台協力者執行跨境鎮壓的具體案例，對少數業者為金錢利益出賣同胞的「背骨惡行」，政府將積極查處、決不寬貸，並加快研議修正《反滲透法》，強化對跨境鎮壓行為的法律規範及處罰。 新北地方檢察署17日偵結一起涉及台灣徵信業者非法蒐集個資案件
content:
【大紀元2026年11月18日訊】（大紀元記者戴德蔓台灣台北報導）台灣徵信業者涉嫌接受中共公安機關指示，非法蒐集網紅「八炯」、「閩南狼」及家屬個資，並派員跟監、拍攝，將情資交付中共公安機關。陸委會11月17日嚴厲譴責，這已非單純個資侵害，而是中共透過在台協力者執行跨境鎮壓的具體案例，對少數業者為金錢利益出賣同胞的「背骨惡行」，政府將積極查處、決不寬貸，並加快研議修正《反滲透法》，強化對跨境鎮壓行為的法律規範及處罰。
新北地方檢察署17日偵結一起涉及台灣徵信業者非法蒐集個資案件。一統及國華徵信社業務經理王秉宏涉嫌接受中國上海市公安局官員指示，非法查詢網紅「八炯」溫子渝、「閩南狼」陳柏源及其家屬個人資料，並指揮人員長期跟監、拍攝活動現場，再將相關情資回傳中國公安機關。檢方依違反《個人資料保護法》起訴王男等3人。
根據檢方調查，王秉宏於2025年3月赴中國期間結識上海市公安局官員，同年6月起接受中共派遣、微信暱稱「廈門阿豪」人士的委託，調查八炯、閩南狼等人的行蹤及基本資料。
檢方指出，王男利用徵信社於2020年間向第三方購買、內含台灣戶役政資料的筆記型電腦，非法查得八炯、閩南狼及其父母親屬共7人的身分證字號、出生日期、戶籍地址、電話及車牌等個資，並將資料回報中國。
針對此案，陸委會17日表示，中共利用台灣徵信業者監控、蒐集民眾個資，再以懸賞通緝等手段打壓持不同政治立場的台灣民眾，不僅侵害台灣民眾的言論自由，更對台灣民主自由秩序造成重大危害。本會對中共進行迫害與跨境鎮壓的惡劣手段，表達最嚴厲的譴責，並要求中共立即停止相關作為。
陸委會指出，根據檢察署偵辦相關案件顯示，近期台灣已有多起徵信業者接受境外勢力指示或委託，從事非法跟監、偷拍及蒐集個資等行為，顯示中共不斷透過在台協力者，將跨境鎮壓的黑手伸入台灣社會。這已非單純的個資侵害案件，而是中共透過在地協力者執行跨境鎮壓的具體案例。
陸委會痛批，面對台灣少數徵信業者及相關人士為了金錢利益，甘受中共指示來出賣同胞、傷害台灣的「背骨惡行」，本會提出嚴正警告，少數業者賣國害台劣跡，政府一定會積極查處，決不寬貸。
陸委會表示，政府已加快反滲透法修法的研議進度，未來將強化對跨境鎮壓行為的法律規範及處罰。本會呼籲朝野各界正視這類犯罪對民眾安全及民主社會的威脅，共同支持相關修法，保障民眾免於境外勢力的恫嚇與威脅。◇

11 月 18 日，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普和菲律宾总统小费迪南德·马科斯在马尼拉马拉卡南宫会晤时握手。

特朗普表示，美国正在扩大与菲律宾的防务合作，已批准超过50亿美元的军售。他表示，联盟“从未如此美好”。
他说华盛顿可以与马尼拉合作开展一个大型民用核能项目。他称这对这两个盟友来说可能是“非常大”的一步。
特朗普还表示，菲律宾可以加入计划中的阿拉斯加天然气出口项目。他表示，两国正在讨论更广泛的能源合作，而他并不担心南海问题。
马尼拉 — — 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普 11 月 18 日告诉菲律宾总统小费迪南德·马科斯，华盛顿正在扩大与其条约盟友的防务合作，还可以与马尼拉合作开展一项重大民用核能项目。
特朗普在前往中国参加亚太经合组织峰会之前正在马尼拉进行国事访问，他表示华盛顿增加了对菲律宾的军事支持，批准了超过50亿美元（64.5亿新元）的军售。
特朗普表示，就菲律宾潜在民用核电项目进行合作可以进一步加强这两个盟友之间的关系。
特朗普表示：“菲律宾在其第一个现代核项目中采用美国技术将凸显两国重要关系的强度，我们可能会在核问题上做一些非常大的事情。”
特朗普表示，菲律宾也可能成为计划中的阿拉斯加天然气出口项目的合作伙伴，并补充说两国正在讨论更广泛的能源合作。
“菲律宾将成为这项努力中非常自然的合作伙伴。我们正在为此努力，”他说。
特朗普还表示，他并不担心有争议的南海局势，并表示美国与菲律宾的联盟从未如此美好。
“我一点也不担心。这会得到解决，”他说。路透社

Trump says US is expanding defence cooperation with Philippines

Trump said the US is expanding defence cooperation with the Philippines, with more than US$5 billion in arms sales approved. He said the alliance is “never been better”.
He said Washington could work with Manila on a major civilian nuclear energy project. He called it a possible “very big” step for the two allies.
Trump also said the Philippines could join a planned Alaska natural gas export project. He said both countries are discussing wider energy cooperation, while he was not worried about the South China Sea.
MANILA – US President Donald Trump told his Philippine counterpart Ferdinand Marcos Jr on Nov 18 that Washington was expanding defence cooperation with its treaty ally and could also work with Manila on a major civilian nuclear energy project.
Trump, who is in Manila on a state visit before heading to China for the APEC summit, said Washington had increased military support for the Philippines, approving more than US$5 billion (S$6.45 billion) in arms sales.
Cooperation on a potential Philippine civilian nuclear power project could further strengthen ties between the two allies, Trump said.
“For the Philippines to embrace American technology in its first modern nuclear project would underscore the strength of the important relationship, and we’re probably going to do something very big to do with nuclear,” Trump said.
Trump said the Philippines could also become a partner in a planned Alaska natural gas export project, adding that the two countries were discussing broader energy cooperation.
“The Philippines would be a very natural partner in this effort. We are working on that,” he said.
Trump also said he was not concerned about the situation in the disputed South China Sea and said the US alliance with the Philippines has never been better.
“I am not concerned at all. That’ll be taken care of,” he said. REUTERS

我们正在确保关键供应链的安全，保护航行和飞越自由，通过未来技术推动增长，包括投资和部署值得信赖的超级智能（SI）*，并通过救生援助应对灾难。我们承诺共同努力，确保印太地区开放、安全和有弹性的海上过境走廊。我们正在与区域伙伴合作，应对共同的挑战并创造机遇，为印太地区带来切实的利益。我们宣布首届四方商界领袖论坛将于 2027 年初举行，来自四方国家的商界领袖、政府官员和政策专家将齐聚一堂，以促进私营部门之间更紧密的商业联系，包括促进对印太地区繁荣至关重要的商业交易和伙伴关系。我们肯定我们的外交部长在亚特兰大宣布的超级情报*加速器的重要性。该加速器旨在协调和资助支持可信超级情报（SI）*在整个印度-太平洋地区的访问、部署和技术援助的努力。我们很自豪地欢迎印度-太平洋海上监视合作，这是一项旨在加强信息共享和海域意识的新举措。 2027年，我们各自的P-8和P-3C巡逻机计划首次在四方背景下进行海上演习，使我们的海洋更加安全。
我们对“电缆连通性和复原力四方伙伴关系”所取得的进展感到自豪，该伙伴关系扩大了整个印度-太平洋地区安全、可信的通信基础设施的覆盖范围。今天，我们欢迎澳大利亚扩大对该伙伴关系的贡献，重点关注电缆，加强区域能源安全和连通性。我们还欢迎即将在印度洋开展的海底电缆项目，该项目旨在加强区域互联互通。我们承认该地区网络事件的数量和规模迅速增加，并宣布加强四方网络安全合作，我们计划通过该合作共同努力
